0880CC00DFE501317E2868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

088082B0DFE501317E2768A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

08803800DFE501317E2668A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

087FDF30DFE501317E2568A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).

087F9210DFE501317E2468A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

087F4B10DFE501317E2368A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

087F0070DFE501317E2268A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

087EA810DFE501317E2168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

087E51F0DFE501317E2068A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

087DF360DFE501317E1F68A86D17958E.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

087DA620DFE501317E1E68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

087D54F0DFE501317E1D68A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

087C31E0DFE501317E1A68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

087BA460DFE501317E1868A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

087B5A70DFE501317E1768A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

087B0880DFE501317E1668A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

087AA920DFE501317E1568A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

087A4640DFE501317E1468A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

0879FB60DFE501317E1368A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

0879A9A0DFE501317E1268A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

08790570DFE501317E1068A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

0878B6D0DFE501317E0F68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

08785F90DFE501317E0E68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

0877C780DFE501317E0C68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

08777560DFE501317E0B68A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

08772260DFE501317E0A68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

0876D380DFE501317E0968A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

087680E0DFE501317E0868A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

0875F2D0DFE501317E0668A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

0875AAA0DFE501317E0568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

0874B8D0DFE501317E0268A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

08746200DFE501317E0168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

0873BC80DFE501317DFF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

08736C50DFE501317DFE68A86D17958E.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

0872C920DFE501317DFC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.

087280A0DFE501317DFB68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.

087235E0DFE501317DFA68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

08717090DFE501317DF868A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.

087112A0DFE501317DF768A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.

0870C700DFE501317DF668A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

086FDD30DFE501317DF368A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

086F8390DFE501317DF268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

086F2C70DFE501317DF168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.

086ED5A0DFE501317DF068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

086DAB70DFE501317DED68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.

086D6070DFE501317DEC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

086D1410DFE501317DEB68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

086C79A0DFE501317DE968A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

086C18C0DFE501317DE868A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.

086BAC50DFE501317DE768A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

086AD910DFE501317DE468A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

086A90E0DFE501317DE368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

086A3AC0DFE501317DE268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

0869F4D0DFE501317DE168A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

0869AE50DFE501317DE068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

document.title: District of Columbia Arts Education Learning Standards

FF5BC150DFE401316E5A68A86D17958E.description: Research and report on what various types of artists (e.g., architects, designers, graphic artists, animators) produce and how their works play a role in our everyday environment.

FF5AF000DFE401316E5868A86D17958E.description: Identify and design icons, logos, and other graphic devices as symbols for ideas and information. Write how the design represents the idea or information.

FF5A2800DFE401316E5668A86D17958E.description: Design a poster that illustrates a theme.

FF59C570DFE401316E5568A86D17958E.description: Interpret an abstract painting relating it to dance/movement.

FF5960D0DFE401316E5468A86D17958E.description: Use linear perspective to depict geometric objects in space.

FF58F220DFE401316E5368A86D17958E.description: Write and illustrate a book (using book arts) implementing the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, editing/proofreading, publishing/presenting) demonstrating a unified drawing style.

FF580F70DFE401316E5168A86D17958E.description: Connect and apply what is learned in the visual arts to other art forms, subject areas, visual culture and communications and to careers. (Connections, Relationships, Applications)

FF57A760DFE401316E5068A86D17958E.description: Using specific criteria, students assess their own works of art and describe what changes they would make for improvement

FF574250DFE401316E4F68A86D17958E.description: Develop and use specific criteria individually and in groups to assess works of art.

FF56DB00DFE401316E4E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how works of art are organized by determining how the principles of design are used and how they affect personal responses and evaluation.

FF567090DFE401316E4D68A86D17958E.description:
Make judgments about works of art and design using a context and critique process involving elements of background history
  • Description (describe)
  • Technical qualities (explain & analyze)
  • Composition (analysis)
  • Meaning, theme, or message (interpret)
  • Perspective on interpretation of subject content
  • Expressive qualities (interpret)Relationship to period or society of origin (investigate/interpret)
  • Significance (judgment)

FF559E40DFE401316E4B68A86D17958E.description: Respond to, analyze, and make judgments about works in the visual arts. (Aesthetics, Valuing & Perspectives of Art)

FF553E60DFE401316E4A68A86D17958E.description: Research the role of visual art and arts during the Harlem Renaissance, exploring how visual arts reflect society and relate to other art forms (e.g. music, dance & theatre).

FF54D730DFE401316E4968A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe how various cultures define and value art differently

FF546E90DFE401316E4868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the visual languages used in the fine art, advertising and propaganda of the World War II era.

FF540470DFE401316E4768A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare works of American art and architecture that show regional differences. View and discuss original examples that can be seen at a major local art museum, such as the National Building Museum, the Smithsonian American Art Museum or the Corcoran Art Gallery.

FF538BB0DFE401316E4668A86D17958E.description: Relate six works in the arts chronologically to historical events (e.g., 10,000 B.C. to present)

FF531D50DFE401316E4568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast images of industrialization, discussing how they celebrate or criticize its impact.

FF52B160DFE401316E4468A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe examples of African-American art and architecture, explaining how African-American artwork reflects multicultural West African and European-American art and societies.

FF524930DFE401316E4368A86D17958E.description: Describe, compare, and contrast various depictions of the American West, posing relevant questions about the perspectives of the artists.

FF51E160DFE401316E4268A86D17958E.description: Historical Development, Role and Cultural Diversity of the Visual Arts

FF517630DFE401316E4168A86D17958E.description: Investigate and understand historical and cultural dimensions of the visual arts and to construct meaning in the diverse ways in which human experience is expressed across time and place. (Historical and Cultural Context)

FF511000DFE401316E4068A86D17958E.description: Communicate values, opinions, and/or personal insights in an original work of art.

FF50A2E0DFE401316E3F68A86D17958E.description: Use the principles of unity and harmony to create an assemblage (a found object sculpture) or a mixed media two-dimensional composition that communicates a universal theme.

FF4FC990DFE401316E3D68A86D17958E.description: Create an expressive abstract composition based on real objects using line characteristics (e.g. straight/curved. thick/thin/zigzag).

FF4F6010DFE401316E3C68A86D17958E.description: Expression Through Original Works of Art

FF4EF320DFE401316E3B68A86D17958E.description: Maintain the workspace, materials, and tools responsibly and safely.

FF4E78E0DFE401316E3A68A86D17958E.description: Experiment with digital imagery (e.g., computer-generated art, digital photography, or videography).

FF498B30DFE401316E2E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe works of art using one-point perspective.

  • percussion: multiple mallets and auxiliary instrument techniques, technique on two timpani
  • strings: shifting (violin/viola up to third position; cello/bass up to fourth position), alternate fingerings, vibrato).

FE9AEA50DFE401316CF968A86D17958E.description: Perform a chromatic scale, ascending and descending, in eighth notes (M.M. quarter note = 72) (for wind/percussion students).

FE9A8230DFE401316CF868A86D17958E.description: Perform The Thirteen Essential Rudiments from the National Association of Rudimental Drummers (NARD), open-close-open (for Percussion students).

FE9A18B0DFE401316CF768A86D17958E.description:
Perform selected major scales ascending and descending in eighth notes (M.M. quarter note = 72):
  • winds: D, G, C, F, Bb, Eb, Ab, Db
  • violin: C, G, D, A, Bb, Ab, two octaves
  • viola/cello: C, G, D, E, F, Eb, two octaves
  • string bass: C, G, D, A, E, F, Bb, Ab, one octave.

FE99A4E0DFE401316CF668A86D17958E.description:
Demonstrate a variety of articulations or bowings:
  • wind: staccato, legato tongue, accent, marcato, tenuto
  • strings: staccato, brush stroke, hooked bowings, martelé, marcato, tremolo, multiple-note slurs.

FE9922A0DFE401316CF568A86D17958E.description: Incorporate tempo changes and a variety of rhythms and meters in materials being studied.

FE98BF60DFE401316CF468A86D17958E.description: Produce tones that are clear, free of tension, sustained, and unwavering in pitch.

FE9859F0DFE401316CF368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate proper playing position through posture, embouchure and hand position, and proper instrument assembly.

FE9778D0DFE401316CF168A86D17958E.description: Sing a part while other students sing contrasting parts.

FE964C30DFE401316CEE68A86D17958E.description: Perform music from a variety of cultures, styles, and historical periods.

FE95E5A0DFE401316CED68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate musical phrasing (melodic contour, natural accents, use of breath or bow) in materials being studied.

FE9583B0DFE401316CEC68A86D17958E.description: Use dynamic contrast as a means of expression.

FE9520F0DFE401316CEB68A86D17958E.description: Perform a one-octave chromatic scale, ascending and descending (for Wind/Percussion students).

FE94B8B0DFE401316CEA68A86D17958E.description: Perform six (long roll, five stroke roll, nine stroke roll, flam, single paradiddle, ruff) of The Thirteen Essential Rudiments from the National Association of Rudimental Drummers (NARD), open-closeopen (for Percussion students).

FE944140DFE401316CE968A86D17958E.description:
Perform four major scales ascending and descending, one octave:
  • winds and percussion: F, Bb, Eb, Ab
  • strings: D, G, C, F.

FE93D4A0DFE401316CE868A86D17958E.description:
Use contrasting articulation:
  • winds: tonguing, slurring
  • strings: détaché, pizzicato, slurring.

FE937330DFE401316CE768A86D17958E.description: Maintain a steady tempo while performing materials being studied.

FE930E80DFE401316CE668A86D17958E.description: Produce tones that are clear and sustained.

FE92A000DFE401316CE568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate proper playing position through posture, embouchure and hand position, and proper instrument assembly.

FE91A400DFE401316CE368A86D17958E.description: Sing selected lines from the material being studied.

FE906650DFE401316CE068A86D17958E.description: Sing and perform on instruments, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

FE8FFC90DFE401316CDF68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate and improve personal performance by comparison with an exemplary model.

FE8F1840DFE401316CDD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a specific work and discuss how the music elements are used to create expression.

FE8EA110DFE401316CDC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ensemble skills blending instrumental timbres; matching dynamic levels, style, and intonation; responding to conducting gestures; using conducting gestures.

FE8E27E0DFE401316CDB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to adjust and match pitches.

FE8CE420DFE401316CD868A86D17958E.description: Diagnose and correct personal performance errors.

FE8BE430DFE401316CD668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ensemble skills blending instrumental timbres; matching dynamic levels, style, and intonation; responding to conducting gestures; using conducting gestures.

FE8B77D0DFE401316CD568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to adjust and match pitches.

FE8A56C0DFE401316CD268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate individual and group performance by offering suggestions for improvement.

FE898530DFE401316CD068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ensemble skills by blending instrumental timbres; matching dynamic levels, style, and intonation; and responding to conducting gestures.

FE8920C0DFE401316CCF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to adjust and match pitches.

FE87E370DFE401316CCC68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate individual and group performance by offering suggestions for improvement.

FE86F850DFE401316CCA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ensemble skills by blending instrumental timbres, matching dynamic levels, responding to basic conducting gestures, and maintaining a steady tempo.

FE867180DFE401316CC968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to adjust pitch while playing an instrument.

FE8546B0DFE401316CC668A86D17958E.description: Listen to, analyze, and evaluate music.

FE8471E0DFE401316CC468A86D17958E.description: Listen to and identify, by genre or style, examples of music from various historical periods and world cultures.

FE840D60DFE401316CC368A86D17958E.description: Describe in writing the roles of musicians in each of the four periods of music history (e.g., Baroque, Classical, Romantic and Contemporary) and include a composer and composition representative of each period.

FE834290DFE401316CC168A86D17958E.description: Produce sound fundamentals for classroom instruments.

FE82DB80DFE401316CC068A86D17958E.description: Identify the use of similar elements in music and other art forms (e.g., form, pattern, rhythm).

FE81F240DFE401316CBE68A86D17958E.description: Connect music to other art forms and subject areas through understanding the historical and cultural context of music.

FE819100DFE401316CBD68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and construct basic chords and chord patterns (e.g., I, V, and V7).

FE811890DFE401316CBC68A86D17958E.description: Use standard symbols to notate meter, rhythm, pitch, and dynamics in song.

FE809CC0DFE401316CBB68A86D17958E.description: Read (sing) melodic notation in treble clef in major keys and minor keys, using solfege.

FE803580DFE401316CBA68A86D17958E.description: Read (using rhythmic solfege) rhythmic notation, including sixteenth notes, dotted notes, and syncopation (e.g., eighth/quarter/eighth note and eighth-rest/quarter/eighth note).

FE7F7110DFE401316CB868A86D17958E.description: Improvise and compose short songs and/or instrumental pieces in duple and triple meter using the following musical devises: imitation and repetition.

FE7F0230DFE401316CB768A86D17958E.description: Improvise, compose, and arrange music to accompany readings and dramatizations.

FE7E9250DFE401316CB668A86D17958E.description: Improvise, compose, and arrange basic rhythmic, melodic and harmonic patterns on classroom instruments and available technology.

FE7E2A70DFE401316CB568A86D17958E.description: Improvise, compose, and arrange simple melodies on a given scale (e.g., pentatonic).

FE7D4C50DFE401316CB368A86D17958E.description: Maintain instruments, voice, performance and practice areas carefully and responsibly.

FE7CD530DFE401316CB268A86D17958E.description: Accompany singing with rhythm and/or melody instruments.

FE7C6F80DFE401316CB168A86D17958E.description: Perform independent instrumental parts while other students sing or play contrasting parts.

FE7C0AF0DFE401316CB068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate embouchure and breath control, bowing or drumstick grip to produce tones on instruments.

FE7B9DB0DFE401316CAF68A86D17958E.description: Perform melodies and accompaniments from a varied repertoire of music from diverse cultures, including rounds, descants, ostinatos, and two-part harmony, by oneself and with others, on classroom instruments.

FE7AAAC0DFE401316CAD68A86D17958E.description: Sing in groups, blending vocal timbres, dynamic levels, and respond to the cues of the conductor.

FE7A44B0DFE401316CAC68A86D17958E.description: Sing with accurate pitch, rhythm, diction, and posture, maintaining a steady tempo.

FE79DF80DFE401316CAB68A86D17958E.description: Sing from memory a varied repertoire of songs representing diverse genres, styles and cultures, including rounds/canons, descants, and songs with ostinatos and songs in two-part harmony, alone and with others.

FE791140DFE401316CA968A86D17958E.description: Sing and perform on instruments alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

FE78AFE0DFE401316CA868A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze difference in tempo and dynamics in contrasting music selections.

FE783E00DFE401316CA768A86D17958E.description: Devise and apply specific criteria for evaluating performances and compositions.

FE775360DFE401316CA568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate perceptual skills by listening to and comparing and contrasting music of various styles and cultures.

FE76E5F0DFE401316CA468A86D17958E.description: Identify vocal and instrumental ensembles from a variety of genres and cultures (e.g., classical, jazz, blues, gamelan, mariachi, cambia, salsa, mambo, reggae).

FE768660DFE401316CA368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how musical sounds are used in various genres and culture.

FE762020DFE401316CA268A86D17958E.description: Define the special properties of musical sounds (pitch, duration, volume and timbre).

FE754240DFE401316CA068A86D17958E.description: Listen to, analyze, and evaluate music.

FE748680DFE401316C9E68A86D17958E.description: Explore the function of dance in daily life in different countries and historic time periods.

FE741DC0DFE401316C9D68A86D17958E.description: Journal the creative and artistic processes of choreographing a dance (the images and ideas to be communicated, how artistic choices were decided, problems that needed to be solved).

FE73B430DFE401316C9C68A86D17958E.description: Create dance studies based on the relationships between dance concepts and concepts from other subjects (force and motion, the body systems, maps and grids, narrative style).

FE735500DFE401316C9B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how dance terminology relates to and shares the vocabulary of other art subjects (such as, shape, line, positive and negative space, rhythm, and phrase.)

FE72F200DFE401316C9A68A86D17958E.description: Interconnect - Apply dance and movement concepts to construct meaning and understanding in the arts, other subject areas, literacy, historical periods, and multiple cultures.

FE728860DFE401316C9968A86D17958E.description: Observe a dance and analyze how the movement fulfills the intent of the choreographer. Suggest additional movement possibilities.

FE722350DFE401316C9868A86D17958E.description: Observe dance performed in several different dance genres and, either orally or in writing, compare and contrast their use of space, time, and energy.

FE71B9E0DFE401316C9768A86D17958E.description: As an audience member, respect and honor the dancer for their devoted work in training, rehearsing, and performing dance.

FE715710DFE401316C9668A86D17958E.description: Explore the life and work of several famous dancers or choreographers from different dance genres. Articulate in dance terminology, either orally or in writing, the similarities and differences in the dance genres.

FE70EA00DFE401316C9568A86D17958E.description: Respond - Analyze, critique, and respond to dance.

FE706AA0DFE401316C9468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate safe and respectful practices and relationships during movement activities when working with a partner or group.

FE6FD6A0DFE401316C9368A86D17958E.description: Remember, perform, reflect, and revise the performance of choreographed dances demonstrating focused concentration, kinesthetic awareness, and responsibility for one's role in a dance.

FE6F5500DFE401316C9268A86D17958E.description: Identify anatomical terminology for major bones, muscles and joints and understand how they allow for efficient movement, balance, flexibility, coordination, and physical control.

FE6EF4D0DFE401316C9168A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance that uses changes in dynamics (energy) to reflect different, ideas, feelings, and meaning.

FE6E8E60DFE401316C9068A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance that demonstrates musicality, including accuracy in moving to a musical beat and responding to changes in tempo and phrasing.

FE6E27A0DFE401316C8F68A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance that uses a variety of levels, directions, pathways, and shapes.

FE6DC870DFE401316C8E68A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance that uses inventive combinations of axial (non-locomotor) and locomotor movements.

FE6D4AC0DFE401316C8D68A86D17958E.description: Perform - Demonstrate dance fundamentals and skills with technical proficiency and spatial, musical, and kinesthetic awareness.

FE6CB530DFE401316C8C68A86D17958E.description: Research a topic of interest and create a short dance based upon the topic.

FE6C3FD0DFE401316C8B68A86D17958E.description: Create and perform a short expressive dance.

FE6BD180DFE401316C8A68A86D17958E.description: Create a short dance using a common choreographic form (such as narrative, theme and variation, ABA, canon, and call-andresponse) that is frequently used in dance.

FE6B6C20DFE401316C8968A86D17958E.description: Create - Understand and create choreographic forms and meaning in dance.

document.title: District of Columbia Social Studies Standards

0F4EF9F0DFE5013189DC68A86D17958E.description: Students conduct cost-benefit analyses and apply basic economic indicators to analyze the aggregate economic behavior of the U.S. economy.

0F4E9D80DFE5013189DB68A86D17958E.description: Students understand the meaning, implication, and impact of historical events and recognize that events could have taken other directions.

0F4E4960DFE5013189DA68A86D17958E.description: Students interpret past events and issues within the context in which an event unfolded rather than present-day norms and values.

0F4DFCD0DFE5013189D968A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish intended from unintended consequences.

0F4DA690DFE5013189D868A86D17958E.description: Students recognize the complexity of historical causes and effects, including the limitations on determining cause and effect.

0F4D57E0DFE5013189D768A86D17958E.description: Students show the connections, causal and otherwise, between particular historical events and larger social, economic, and political trends and developments.

0F4CEBD0DFE5013189D668A86D17958E.description: Students analyze how change happens at different rates at different times, understand that some aspects can change while others remain the same, and understand that change is complicated and affects not only technology and politics but also values and beliefs.

0F4C8660DFE5013189D568A86D17958E.description: Students compare the present with the past, evaluating the consequences of past events and decisions and determining the lessons that were learned.

0F4C0080DFE5013189D368A86D17958E.description: Students construct and test hypotheses; collect, evaluate, and employ information from multiple primary and secondary sources; and apply it in oral and written presentations.

0F4BBBC0DFE5013189D268A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate major debates among historians concerning alternative interpretations of the past, including an analysis of authors' use of evidence and the distinctions between sound generalizations and misleading oversimplifications.

0F4B7310DFE5013189D168A86D17958E.description: Students identify bias and prejudice in historical interpretations.

0F4B2590DFE5013189D068A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish valid arguments from fallacious arguments in historical interpretations (e.g., appeal to false authority, unconfirmed citations, ad hominem argument, appeal to popular opinion).

0F4AD5B0DFE5013189CF68A86D17958E.description: Historical Research, Evidence, and Point of View

0F4A91B0DFE5013189CE68A86D17958E.description: Students identify patterns and networks of economic interdependence in the contemporary world.

0F4A4CA0DFE5013189CD68A86D17958E.description: Students explain how different points of view influence policies relating to the use and management of Earth's resources.

0F4A03E0DFE5013189CC68A86D17958E.description: Students study current events to explain how human actions modify the physical environment and how the physical environment affects human systems (e.g., natural disasters, climate, and resources). They explain the resulting environmental policy issues.

0F49BA90DFE5013189CB68A86D17958E.description: Students note significant changes in the territorial sovereignty that took place in the history units being studied.

0F496FF0DFE5013189CA68A86D17958E.description: Students hypothesize about the impact of push-pull factors on human migration in selected regions and about the changes in these factors over time. Students develop maps of human migration and settlement patterns at different times in history and compare them to the present.

0F4920D0DFE5013189C968A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate ways in which technology has expanded the capability of humans to modify the physical environment and the ability of humans to mitigate the effect of natural disasters.

0F48DA20DFE5013189C868A86D17958E.description: Students relate current events to the physical and human characteristics of places and regions. They identify the characteristics, distribution, and complexity of Earth's cultural mosaics.

0F488F70DFE5013189C768A86D17958E.description: Students use a variety of maps and documents to interpret human movement, including major patterns of domestic and international migration, changing environmental preferences and settlement patterns, the frictions that develop between population groups, and the diffusion of ideas, technological innovations, and goods. Identify major patterns of human migration, both in the past and present.

0F4843A0DFE5013189C668A86D17958E.description: Students understand the influence of physical and human geographic factors on the evolution of significant historic events and movements. They apply the geographic viewpoint to local, regional, and world policies and problems.

0F47A420DFE5013189C468A86D17958E.description: Historical and Social Sciences Analysis Skills

0F764F70DFE501318A4D68A86D17958E.description: Trace the rise of resistance from Africans, such as Queen Nzingha of Angola and King Maremba of the Congo, the rise of antislavery sentiment and economic circumstances in Britain that led to abolition in 1833, and the rise of legitimate commerce after the abolition of the trans-Atlantic slave trade. (P, S, E)

0F7605E0DFE501318A4C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of slave labor to trans-Atlantic agriculture and commerce supporting the booming capitalist economy of the 17th and 18th centuries, with the greatest demand coming from Brazil and the sugar plantations of the Caribbean. (E)

0F75B370DFE501318A4B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between the slave trade and the political and economic expansion and/or disruptions of various African coastal and inland state (and other governance) formations (e.g., Yoruba, Akan, and Malian large-scale kingdoms, and Ibo and Ki-Kongo small village systems). (P, S, E)

0F754320DFE501318A4A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that millions of Africans were forcibly removed from seven regions in northwestern, central and southwestern, and southeastern Africa as captives and forced to endure the harsh conditions of the Middle Passage. (S)

0F74E4F0DFE501318A4968A86D17958E.description: Students describe patterns of change in Africa during the trade in slaves between Africa, Europe, and the Americas from the 17th through 18th centuries.

0F749EA0DFE501318A4868A86D17958E.description: Describe how nationalism spread across Europe with Napoleon but was repressed for a generation under the Congress of Vienna and Concert of Europe until the Revolutions of 1848. (P)

0F745450DFE501318A4768A86D17958E.description: Describe the initial uprisings against the mother country in Spanish America, describe their takeover by the largely indigenous masses, and explain the outcomes of these movements. (P, I)

0F740270DFE501318A4668A86D17958E.description: Explain how the ideology of the French Revolution led France to evolve from constitutional monarchy to democratic despotism to the Napoleonic Empire. (P, I)

0F73B7B0DFE501318A4568A86D17958E.description: Understand the unique character of the American Revolution, its spread to other parts of the world, and its continuing significance to other nations. (P, I)

0F7369E0DFE501318A4468A86D17958E.description: Explain the significance of the Haitian Revolution (1791–1804). (P, S, I)

0F730BD0DFE501318A4368A86D17958E.description: List and explain the principles of the Magna Carta, the English Bill of Rights (1689), the American Declaration of Independence (1776), the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and the Citizen (1789), and the U.S. Bill of Rights (1791). (P)

0F72B5E0DFE501318A4268A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the major ideas of philosophers and their effects on the democratic revolutions in England, the United States, France, and Latin America (e.g., John Locke, Charles-Louis Montesquieu, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Simón Bolívar, Toussainte L'Ouverture, Thomas Jefferson, and James Madison). (P, I)

0F725990DFE501318A4168A86D17958E.description: Students compare and contrast the Glorious Revolution of England, the American Revolution, the Spanish American Wars of Independence, and the French Revolution, and their enduring effects on the political expectations for self-government and individual liberty.

0F7213C0DFE501318A4068A86D17958E.description: Explain the origins of modern capitalism; the influence of mercantilism and the cottage industry; the elements and importance of a market economy in 17th-century Europe; the changing international trading and marketing patterns, including their locations on a world map; and the influence of explorers and mapmakers. (E)

0F71CD80DFE501318A3F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the accomplishments of major Enlightenment thinkers (e.g., John Locke and Charles-Louis Montesquieu). (P, I)

0F717820DFE501318A3E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the main ideas of the Enlightenment can be traced back to such movements and epochs as the Renaissance, the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, the Greeks, the Romans, and Christianity. (P, I)

0F7129B0DFE501318A3D68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze political, social, and economic change as a result of the Age of Enlightenment in Europe.

0F70D960DFE501318A3C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the significance of new scientific theories, the accomplishments of leading figures (e.g., Bacon, Copernicus, Descartes, Galileo, Kepler, Linnaeus, and Newton), and new inventions (e.g., the telescope, microscope, thermometer, and barometer). (I)

0F7081E0DFE501318A3B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the roots of the Scientific Revolution (e.g., Greek rationalism; Jewish, Christian, and Muslim science; Renaissance humanism; new knowledge from global exploration). (R, I)

0F703880DFE501318A3A68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the historical developments of the Scientific Revolution and its lasting effect on religious, political, and cultural institutions.

0F6FDFB0DFE501318A3968A86D17958E.description: Era VI: The Age of Revolutions

0F682A40DFE501318A2068A86D17958E.description: Trace the growing economic and political power of the British East India Company in key cities on the subcontinent. (P, E)

0F67E730DFE501318A1F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the art and architecture (e.g., the Taj Mahal) during the Mughal period. (I)

0F67A280DFE501318A1E68A86D17958E.description: Characterize the development of the Sikh religion. (R)

0F675C50DFE501318A1D68A86D17958E.description: Trace the influence of the following great Mughal rulers on the subcontinent: Babur, Akbar, and Arangzeb. (P)

0F670E20DFE501318A1C68A86D17958E.description: Students summarize political and social developments on the Indian Subcontinent during the Mughal eras and the beginnings of British political dominance.

0F66BA70DFE501318A1B68A86D17958E.description: Trace the rise of the early Ching Dynasty in China and growing European demand for Chinese goods, such as tea and silk. (P, E)

0F666EC0DFE501318A1A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the influence of a rigid class system, the Samurai elites, and Tokugawa isolationist's policies on Japanese government and society. (P, S)

0F6619E0DFE501318A1968A86D17958E.description: Describe Japan's unification, after years of civil war, and the establishment of centralized feudalism under the Tokugawa shoguns. (P)

0F65C2C0DFE501318A1868A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of European contacts on China and Japan. (G, P)

0F655DB0DFE501318A1768A86D17958E.description: Describe Chinese power and technology through Zheng He's voyages (the Ming Dynasty). (G, P)

0F6505E0DFE501318A1668A86D17958E.description: Students explain political and social developments in China and Japan in an era of expanding European influence.

0F64AAA0DFE501318A1568A86D17958E.description: Describe the exchanges of plants, animals, technology, culture, ideas, and diseases among Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas in the 15th and 16th centuries and the major economic and social effects on each continent. (G, S, E)

0F645E80DFE501318A1468A86D17958E.description: Explain the development and effects of the Atlantic slave trade. (S, E)

0F641370DFE501318A1368A86D17958E.description: Describe the goals and extent of Dutch, English, French, and Spanish settlements in the Americas. (G, P)

0F63C6D0DFE501318A1268A86D17958E.description: Identify the voyages of discovery, the locations of the routes, and the influence of cartography in the development of a new European worldview. (G, I)

0F637670DFE501318A1168A86D17958E.description: Students describe the rise of English Colonial Empires.

0F6F8940DFE501318A3868A86D17958E.description: Explain how that cooperation was terminated by the religious persecution of individuals and groups (e.g., the Spanish Inquisition and the expulsion of Jews and Muslims from Spain). (R, S)

0F6F4640DFE501318A3768A86D17958E.description: Describe the Golden Age of cooperation between Jews and Muslims in medieval Spain that promoted creativity in art, literature, and science. (S, E)

0F6F01C0DFE501318A3668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the Catholic Counter-Reformation revitalized the Catholic Church and the forces that fostered the movement (e.g., St. Ignatius of Loyola and the Jesuits, the Council of Trent). (P, R)1. Identify the voyages of discovery, the locations of the routes, and the influence of cartography in the development of a new European worldview. (G, I)

0F6EBE60DFE501318A3568A86D17958E.description: Explain Protestants' new practices of church self-government and the influence of those practices on the development of democratic practices and ideas of federalism. (P, R)

0F6E79E0DFE501318A3468A86D17958E.description: Outline the reasons for the growing discontent with the Catholic Church, including the main ideas of Martin Luther (salvation by faith) and John Calvin (predestination) and their attempts to reconcile God's word with Church action. (P, R)

0F6E3310DFE501318A3368A86D17958E.description: List and explain the causes for the internal turmoil within and eventual weakening of the Catholic Church (e.g., tax policies, selling of indulgences, England's break with the Catholic Church). (P, R)

0F6DD720DFE501318A3268A86D17958E.description: Explain the supremacy of the Catholic Church, the growth of literacy, the spread of printed books, the explosion of knowledge and the Church's reaction to these developments.

0F6D8EB0DFE501318A3168A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the European regions that remained Catholic and those that became Protestant and how the division affected the distribution of religions in the New World. (G, R)

0F6D44E0DFE501318A3068A86D17958E.description: Explain the institution and impact of missionaries on Christianity and the diffusion of Christianity from Europe to other parts of the world in the medieval and early modern periods. (G, R)

0F6CFB90DFE501318A2F68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the historical developments of the Reformation.

0F6CAE00DFE501318A2E68A86D17958E.description: Outline the advances made in literature, the arts, science, mathematics, cartography, engineering, and the understanding of human anatomy and astronomy (e.g., by Dante Alighieri, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni, Johann Gutenberg, and William Shakespeare). (I)

0F6C5040DFE501318A2D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the growth and effects of new ways of disseminating information (e.g., the ability to manufacture paper, translation of the Bible into vernacular, and printing). (I, S)

0F6BF870DFE501318A2C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the way in which the revival of classical learning and the arts fostered a new interest in humanism (i.e., a balance between intellect and religious faith). (R, I)

0F6BAE50DFE501318A2B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the similarities and differences between the Northern and Southern Renaissance. (P, I)

0F6B5940DFE501318A2A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of the reopening of the ancient Silk Road between Europe and China, including Marco Polo's travels and the location of his routes. (G, E)

0F6B0620DFE501318A2968A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of Florence in the early stages of the Renaissance and the growth of independent trading cities (e.g., Venice) and their importance in the spread of Renaissance ideas. (G, S, E)

0F6AADC0DFE501318A2868A86D17958E.description: Trace the emergence of the Renaissance, including influence from Moorish (or Muslim) scholars in Spain. (G, P, S)

0F6A4870DFE501318A2768A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the origins, accomplishments, and geographic diffusion of the Renaissance.

0F69E8C0DFE501318A2668A86D17958E.description: Describe Shah Abbas and how his policies of cultural blending led to the Golden Age of the Safavid Empire.

0F69A210DFE501318A2568A86D17958E.description: Summarize the rise of the Safavid Empire.

0F6958C0DFE501318A2468A86D17958E.description: Describe the expansion of the Ottoman Empire into North Africa, Eastern Europe, and throughout the Middle East, and describe the importance of the Battle of Lepanto in the 16th century limiting Ottoman ambitions in the Mediterranean. (G, M)

0F690E60DFE501318A2368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the importance of the capture of Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, in 1453. (P, M)

0F68C270DFE501318A2268A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of Mehmed II the Conqueror and Suleiman the Magnificent. (P, M)

0F686DA0DFE501318A2168A86D17958E.description: Students describe the rise of the Ottoman Empire in the 14th, 15th, and 16th centuries.

0F633190DFE501318A1068A86D17958E.description: Era V: Early Modern Times to 1650

0F62EC30DFE501318A0F68A86D17958E.description: Compare the development of these societies to that of other indigenous societies in North America, the Caribbean, or others in Mesoamerica or the Andes.

0F62A560DFE501318A0E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the Mesoamerican developments in astronomy and mathematics, including the calendar, and the Mesoamerican knowledge of seasonal changes to the civilizations' agricultural systems. (I)

0F625B10DFE501318A0D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the artistic and oral traditions and architecture in the three civilizations. (S, I)

0F620260DFE501318A0C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the roles of people in each society, including class structures, family life, warfare, religious beliefs and practices, and slavery. (S, R, E)

0F61B490DFE501318A0B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how and where each empire arose (how the Aztec and Incan empires were eventually defeated by the Spanish in the 16th century). (P, M)

0F616940DFE501318A0A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the highly structured social and political system of the Maya civilization, ruled by nobles and kings and consisting of many independent politically sovereign states. (P)

0F6117A0DFE501318A0968A86D17958E.description: Locate and explain the locations, landforms, and climates of Mexico, Central America, and South America and their effects on Mayan, Aztec, and Incan economies, trade, and development of urban societies. (G, E)

0F60CA50DFE501318A0868A86D17958E.description: Students compare and contrast the geographic, political, religious, social, and economic structures of the Mesoamerican and Andean civilizations.

0F59DCD0DFE5013189FF68A86D17958E.description: Outline the decline of Muslim rule in the Iberian Peninsula that culminated in the Reconquista and the rise of Spanish and Portuguese kingdoms. (P, M)

0F606E20DFE501318A0768A86D17958E.description: Explain the initial emergence of a modern economy, including the growth of banking, technological and agricultural improvements, commerce, towns, and a merchant class. (E)

0F5EB840DFE501318A0668A86D17958E.description: Describe the economic and social effects of the spread of the bubonic plague from Central Asia to China, the Middle East, and Europe, and its impact on global population. (G, S, E)

0F5BA6D0DFE501318A0568A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of the Catholic Church as a political, intellectual, and aesthetic institution (e.g., founding of universities, political and spiritual roles of the clergy, creation of monastic and mendicant religious orders, preservation of the Latin language and religious texts, St. Thomas Aquinas's synthesis of classical philosophy with Christian theology, and the concept of "natural law"). (P, R, I)

0F5B5FF0DFE501318A0468A86D17958E.description: Describe the causes, course, and consequences of the European Crusades against Islam and their effects on the Christian, Muslim, and Jewish populations in Europe, with emphasis on the increasing contact by Europeans with cultures of the Eastern Mediterranean world. (P, R, M)

0F5B18F0DFE501318A0368A86D17958E.description: Describe the spread of Christianity north of the Alps and the roles played by the early church and by monasteries in its diffusion after the fall of the western half of the Roman Empire. (R)

0F5ACBE0DFE501318A0268A86D17958E.description: Explain the significance of developments in medieval English legal and constitutional practices and their importance in the rise of modern democratic thought and representative institutions (e.g., trial by jury, the common law, Magna Carta, parliament, habeas corpus, and an independent judiciary in England). (P, I)

0F5A7830DFE501318A0168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the conflict and cooperation between the Papacy and European monarchs (e.g., Charlemagne, Gregory VII, and Emperor Henry IV), the disputes over papal authority, and the Great Schism. (P, R, I)

0F5A2800DFE501318A0068A86D17958E.description: Describe the development of feudalism and manorialism, its role in the medieval European economy, the way in which it was influenced by physical geography (the role of the manor and the growth of towns), and how feudal relationships provided the foundation of political order and private property ownership. (G, P, E)

0F598C70DFE5013189FE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the geography of Europe and the Eurasian landmass, including their location, topography, waterways, vegetation, and climate, and their relationship to ways of life in medieval Europe. (G, S)

0F5936A0DFE5013189FD68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the geographic, political, religious, social, and economic structures of the civilizations of medieval Europe.

0F58DFB0DFE5013189FC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of Mansa Musa and his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324. (P, R, E)

0F588A70DFE5013189FB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the importance of family, labor specialization, and regional commerce in the development of states and cities in West Africa. (S, E)

0F583650DFE5013189FA68A86D17958E.description: Trace the rise to prominence of Sundiata Keita, the legendary founder of the empire of Mali. (P)

0F57D7E0DFE5013189F968A86D17958E.description: Describe the importance of written and oral traditions in the transmission of African history and culture. (S, I)

0F578200DFE5013189F868A86D17958E.description: Trace the growth of the Arabic language in government, trade, and Islamic scholarship in West Africa. (P, S, I)

0F573DC0DFE5013189F768A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of the trans-Saharan caravan trade in the changing religious and cultural characteristics of West Africa and the influence of Islamic beliefs, ethics, and law. (G, R, S)

0F56F7D0DFE5013189F668A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the site of these civilizations, the importance of the Niger River, and the relationship between vegetation zones of forest, savannah, and desert to the trade in gold, salt, food, and slaves. Illustrate the growth of the Ghana, Mali, and Songhai kingdoms/empires (e.g., trading centers such as Timbuktu and Jenne, which would later develop into important centers of culture and learning). (G, E, I)

0F56B320DFE5013189F568A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the geographic, political, religious, social, and economic structures of the sub-Saharan civilizations of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai of West Africa in the Middle Ages.

0F566E60DFE5013189F468A86D17958E.description: Describe the Kamakura and Ashikaga Shogunates, the rise of warrior governments, and Japanese political disunity. (P)

0F5626D0DFE5013189F368A86D17958E.description: Describe how the Heian (contemporary Kyoto) aristocracy created enduring Japanese cultural perspectives that are epitomized in works of prose such as The Tale of Genji, one of the world's first novels. (S, I)

0F55D720DFE5013189F268A86D17958E.description: Trace the emergence of the Japanese nation during the Nara (710–794) and Heian periods (794–1180). (P)

0F557B70DFE5013189F168A86D17958E.description: Explain the influence of China and the Korean peninsula upon Japan as Buddhism, Confucianism, and the Chinese writing system were adopted. (G, P, R)

0F553560DFE5013189F068A86D17958E.description: Explain the major features of Shinto, Japan's indigenous religion. (R)

0F54EBF0DFE5013189EF68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the geographic, political, religious, social, and economic structures of the civilizations of medieval Japan.

0F54A280DFE5013189EE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the Mongol conquest of China. (M, P)

0F5448D0DFE5013189ED68A86D17958E.description: Trace the spread of Chinese technology — such as papermaking, wood-block printing, the compass, and gunpowder — to other parts of Asia, the Islamic world, and Europe. (S, I, E)

0F53F2E0DFE5013189EC68A86D17958E.description: Describe rapid agricultural, commercial, and technological development during the Song dynasties. (G, E)

0F5390B0DFE5013189EB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the development of a Confucian-based examination system and imperial bureaucracy and its stabilizing political influence. (P, R, S)

0F534A00DFE5013189EA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the reunification of China under the Tang Dynasty and reasons for the spread of Buddhism in Tang China, Korea, and Japan. (P, R)

0F52FDE0DFE5013189E968A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the physical location and major geographical features of China. (G)

0F52B140DFE5013189E868A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious, and social structures of the civilizations of China in the Middle Ages.

0F5262B0DFE5013189E768A86D17958E.description: Describe the establishment of trade routes among Asia, Africa, and Europe; the role of the Mongols in increasing Euro-Asian trade; the products and inventions that traveled along these routes (e.g., spices, textiles, paper, steel, and new crops); and the role of merchants in Arab society. (G, I, E)

0F5215A0DFE5013189E668A86D17958E.description: Describe the growth of thriving cities as centers of Islamic art and learning, such as Cordoba and Baghdad.

0F51C440DFE5013189E568A86D17958E.description: Explain the intellectual exchanges among Muslim scholars of Eurasia and Africa and the contributions Muslim scholars made to later civilizations during the Islamic Golden Age in the areas of science, alchemy, geography, mathematics (algebra), philosophy, art, and literature. (I)

0F517C90DFE5013189E468A86D17958E.description: Trace the origins and impact of different sects within Islam, including the sources of disagreement between Suunis and Shi'ites. (R, P)

0F513750DFE5013189E368A86D17958E.description: Explain the significance of the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the primary sources of Islamic beliefs, practice, and law, and their influence in Muslims' daily life. (R, S)

0F50F220DFE5013189E268A86D17958E.description: Trace the origins of Islam and the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, including Islamic teachings on its connection with Judaism and Christianity. (G, R)

0F50A970DFE5013189E168A86D17958E.description: Describe the expansion of Muslim rule through military conquests and treaties, emphasizing the cultural blending within Muslim civilization (Phoenician and Persian) and the spread and acceptance of Islam and the Arabic language. (P, R, M, S)

0F505890DFE5013189E068A86D17958E.description: Identify the physical location and features and the climate of the Arabian Peninsula, its relationship to surrounding bodies of land and water, and nomadic and sedentary ways of life. (G)

0F5001A0DFE5013189DF68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, social, and religious structures of the civilizations of Islam in the Middle Ages.

0F4F6210DFE5013189DD68A86D17958E.description: World History and Geography I: Middle Ages to the Age of Revolutions

document.title: District of Columbia Science Standards

0C24C680DFE50131845668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that entire species may prosper in spite of the poor survivability or bad fortune of individuals.

0C271FD0DFE50131845E68A86D17958E.description: Describe that all organisms, including the human species, are part of and depend on two main interconnected global food webs: the ocean food web and the land food web.

0C26DE10DFE50131845D68A86D17958E.description: Explain why in urban environments a species (mostly human beings) settles in dense concentrations.

0C269920DFE50131845C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how, as any population of organisms grows, it is held in check by one or more environmental constraints (e.g., depletion of food or nesting sites, increased numbers of predators or parasites).

0C264460DFE50131845B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how dead plants and animals, broken down by other living organisms (especially microorganisms and fungi), contribute to the cycling of matter through the system as a whole.

0C25FCE0DFE50131845A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms that eat plants break down the plant structures to produce the materials and energy that they need to survive, and in turn, other organisms consume them.

0C25B7E0DFE50131845968A86D17958E.description: Create a food web to explain how energy and matter are transferred between producers, primary consumers, and secondary consumers.

0C256DC0DFE50131845868A86D17958E.description: Illustrate and explain how plants use the energy from light to make simple sugars, and more complex molecules, from carbon dioxide and water through a process called photosynthesis. Understand how this produces food that can be used immediately or stored for later use.

0C251420DFE50131845768A86D17958E.description: Describe how two types of organisms may interact in a competitive or cooperative relationship, such as producer/consumer, predator/prey, parasite/hosts, or as symbionts.

0C2474C0DFE50131845568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in all environments, such as freshwater, marine, forest, desert, grassland, mountain, farms, cities, and others, organisms with similar needs and living strategies compete with one another for resources, including food, space, water, air, and shelter.

0C242C10DFE50131845468A86D17958E.description: Organisms in ecosystems exchange energy and nutrients among themselves and with the physical environment. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C211DE0DFE50131844A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how fundamental changes in health practices have resulted from the establishment of the germ theory of disease.

0C238C80DFE50131845268A86D17958E.description: Research and explain the contributions of key scientists that have studied infection by disease organisms (germs), including Anton van Leeuwenhoek, Louis Pasteur, Joseph Lister, Robert Koch, Dimitri Iwanowski, and Alexander Fleming.

0C2324A0DFE50131845168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the environment may contain dangerous levels of substances that are harmful to human beings. Therefore, the good health of individuals requires monitoring the soil, air, and water, as well as taking steps to keep them safe.

0C22C8B0DFE50131845068A86D17958E.description: Know that antibodies produced in response to an invader can remain for long periods in the system and can fight off subsequent invaders of the same kind.

0C228360DFE50131844F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how white blood cells engulf invaders or produce antibodies that attack invaders or mark the invaders for killing by other white blood cells. Know that these white cells are part of a larger system that produces "immunity" or the capacity to resist disease due to pathogens.

0C224120DFE50131844E68A86D17958E.description: Identify specific examples of how viruses, bacteria, fungi, and more complex parasites may infect the human body and interfere with normal body functions.

0C21FDB0DFE50131844D68A86D17958E.description: Research and explain that regular exercise is important to maintain a healthy heart/lung (cardiovascular) system, good muscle tone, and strong bone structure.

0C21B950DFE50131844C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the amount of food energy (usually measured in calories) that a person requires varies with body weight, age, sex, activity level, and metabolic rate.

0C216950DFE50131844B68A86D17958E.description: Explain that human beings have many similarities and differences, and the similarities make it possible for human beings to donate blood and organs to one another.

0C20D9A0DFE50131844968A86D17958E.description: Describe the specific functions and roles of each major human body system, including the digestive, respiratory, excretory, reproductive, circulatory, nervous, endocrine, musculoskeletal, and immune systems.

0C209610DFE50131844868A86D17958E.description: Human beings have body systems for obtaining and providing energy, defense, reproduction, and the coordination of body functions. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C200EC0DFE50131844668A86D17958E.description: Using specific examples, explain that extinction of a species is a result of mismatch of adaptation and the environment.

0C1FC5C0DFE50131844568A86D17958E.description: Explain how independent lines of evidence drawn from geology, fossils, comparative anatomy, and molecular biology provide the firm basis of evolutionary theory.

0C1F67B0DFE50131844468A86D17958E.description: Describe how biological evolution results primarily from the action of natural selection on the available variation in a population of organisms.

0C1F1C40DFE50131844368A86D17958E.description: Explain how Darwin's research and that of his followers supported a concept of differential survival in terms of fitness (i.e., given the potential exponential increase of offspring and the only linear potential increase of resources, favorable variations that aid individual organisms in their survival in a given environment will confer on those organisms a greater reproductive success for that variety).

0C1ECE10DFE50131844268A86D17958E.description: Describe that biological variation (phenotype variation) is the raw material on which natural selection operates.

0C1E74B0DFE50131844168A86D17958E.description: Biological evolution accounts for the diversity of species developed through gradual processes over many generations. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C1DD990DFE50131843F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the use of genetic-engineering techniques can speed the process of creating new varieties and introduce characteristics not easily available by selective breeding, and can make possible more precise modifications involving the manipulation of just one or a few genes.

0C1D7B50DFE50131843E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe that new varieties of cultivated plants, such as corn and apples, and domestic animals, such as dogs and horses, have resulted from selective breeding, over multiple generations, for particular traits.

0C1D0F10DFE50131843D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how, in sexual reproduction, a single reproductive cell from a female (female gamete, egg, or ovum) merges with a specialized cell from a male (male gamete or spermatozoon) to make a fertilized egg (zygote). This carries genetic information from both parental gametes and multiplies to form the complete organism.

0C1CC610DFE50131843C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how, in asexual reproduction, offspring are an almost identical copy of the mother cell.

0C1C8130DFE50131843B68A86D17958E.description: Describe that heredity is the passage of information for developing and maintaining the organism's body from one generation to another, and that genes are the basic units of heredity; genes are made of DNA, consisting of very long molecules located in the chromosomes of each cell.

0C1C3810DFE50131843A68A86D17958E.description: Every organism requires information in the form of a set of instructions that specifies its traits. Those traits may be modified by environmental influences. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C193F00DFE50131843068A86D17958E.description: Construct a chart and describe that multicellular organisms are organized hierarchically from cells to tissues to organs to organ systems to organisms.

0C18FF80DFE50131842F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that many organisms are single-celled (e.g., bacteria, yeasts), and explain how this one cell must carry out all of the basic functions of life.

0C1B9AB0DFE50131843868A86D17958E.description: Explain how cells in multicellular organisms continually divide to make more cells for growth and repair, and how various organs and tissues function to serve the needs of cells for food, air, and waste removal.

0C1B56B0DFE50131843768A86D17958E.description: Describe how the most basic chemical functions of organisms, such as extracting energy from food and getting rid of wastes, are started or carried out completely within the cell.

0C1B1210DFE50131843668A86D17958E.description: Observe and explain that about two-thirds of the mass of a typical cell is accounted for by water and that water gives cells many of their properties.

0C1ACD70DFE50131843568A86D17958E.description: Describe that plant cells have chloroplasts and a cellulose cell wall and that animal cells do not.

0C1A86C0DFE50131843468A86D17958E.description: Know intracellular bodies with specific functions are called organelles. Describe the important organelles among them, such as mitochondria, which liberate energy for the work that cells do, and chloroplasts, which capture sunlight energy for photosynthesis.

0C1A3D60DFE50131843368A86D17958E.description: Identify cells such as bacteria and blue-green algae as prokaryotes. Explain that prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells most prominently in that they don't have a membrane-bound nucleus. Know their genetic information is in a threadlike mass, often a very long loop of DNA.

0C19D8F0DFE50131843268A86D17958E.description: Explain that in those cells that contain a nucleus (eukaryotic plant and animal cells), the nucleus is the main repository for genetic information.

0C198C10DFE50131843168A86D17958E.description: Describe that the way in which cells function is similar in all living organisms.

0C18BEB0DFE50131842E68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and explain that all living things are composed of one or more cells, that cells are organisms' basic units of structure and function, and that cells come only from existing cells (Theodor Schwann's and Matthias Schleiden's cell theory).

0C187B50DFE50131842D68A86D17958E.description: All living things are composed of cells, from just one to many quadrillions, whose details usually are visible only through a microscope. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C17D470DFE50131842B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how similarities among organisms are found in external and internal anatomical features, including specific characteristics at the cellular level, such as the number of chromosomes.

0C178560DFE50131842A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the definition of a species as a group or population of organisms closely resembling one another that can mate and breed to produce fertile offspring.

0C174390DFE50131842968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe that biological classifications are based on how organisms are related: Organisms are classified into a hierarchy of groups and subgroups, with species as the most fundamental unit.

0C1703D0DFE50131842868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe that a key distinction among organisms is between autotrophs, such as green plants (which use energy from sunlight to make their own food), and heterotrophs, such as animals and fungi (which consume other organisms as food and harvest energy from them).

0C16C350DFE50131842768A86D17958E.description: Similarities are used to classify organisms since they may be used to infer the degree of relatedness among organisms. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0C163A60DFE50131842568A86D17958E.description: Know how technologies having to do with food production, sanitation, and disease prevention have dramatically changed how people live and work, and have resulted in changes in factors that affect the growth of human population.

0C15E260DFE50131842468A86D17958E.description: Explain types of technology that are developed and in use, such as in agriculture, manufacturing, sanitation, medicine, warfare, transportation, information processing, and communication.

0C15A360DFE50131842368A86D17958E.description: Although each of the human enterprises of science and technology has a character and history of its own, each is dependent on and reinforces the other. Students:

0C152800DFE50131842168A86D17958E.description: Question claims based on vague attributes or on authority, such as "leading doctors say," or based on statements made by celebrities or others outside the area of their particular expertise.

0C14E9B0DFE50131842068A86D17958E.description: Recognize whether evidence is consistent with a proposed explanation. Know that different explanations can be given for the same evidence, and that partial evidence may be exploited for reasons other than truth seeking.

0C14AA50DFE50131841F68A86D17958E.description: Incorporate circle charts, bar and line graphs, diagrams, scatter plots, and symbols into writing, such as lab or research reports, to serve as visual displays of evidence for claims and/or conclusions.

0C146740DFE50131841E68A86D17958E.description: Communicate the steps and results from an investigation in written reports and verbal presentations.

0C140340DFE50131841D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize testable hypotheses in investigations that pertain to the content under study, and write instructions that others can follow in carrying out the investigation.

0C13B120DFE50131841C68A86D17958E.description: Explain why research involving human subjects requires that potential subjects be fully informed about the risks and benefits associated with the research and that they have the right to refuse to participate.

0C135FE0DFE50131841B68A86D17958E.description: Explain why it is important in science to keep honest, clear, and accurate records.

0C131070DFE50131841A68A86D17958E.description: Explain that when similar investigations give different results, further studies may help to show whether the differences are significant.

0C12C060DFE50131841968A86D17958E.description: Scientific progress is made by asking relevant questions and conducting careful investigations. As a basis for understanding this concept, and to address the content in this grade, students should develop their own questions and perform investigations. Students:

document.title: District of Columbia Arts Education Learning Standards

0461D8F0DFE50131764D68A86D17958E.description: Research and participate in pre-college programs, (e.g. student portfolio days) at colleges and universities, such as the Corcoran College of Art and Design.

046160D0DFE50131764C68A86D17958E.description: Develop career tools such as a professional quality portfolio, a resume, cover letters, and competition entries.

0460E1D0DFE50131764B68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and report on the essential features of modern or emerging technologies that affect or will affect visual artists and the definition of the visual arts.

04606260DFE50131764A68A86D17958E.description: Research visual arts and design careers and post-secondary institutions that provide training.

032B6AE0DFE50131742B68A86D17958E.description: Compose music in several distinct styles, demonstrating creativity in using the elements of music (pitch, rhythm, harmony, dynamics, timbre, texture, form) for expressive effect.

032A01E0DFE50131742868A86D17958E.description: Improvise rhythmic and melodic variations on given pentatonic melodies and melodies in major and minor keys.

03289CF0DFE50131742568A86D17958E.description: Perform on one or more instruments, a large and varied repertoire of instrumental literature, representing various genres, styles, and cultures, and demonstrate technical accuracy, tone quality and articulation, by oneself and in ensembles (level of difficulty: 5 on a scale of 1-6).

0327B010DFE50131742368A86D17958E.description: Perform instrumental literature, representing various genres, styles, and cultures, and demonstrate technical accuracy, tone quality and articulation (level of difficulty: 4 on a scale of 1-6) on one or more instruments.

03263160DFE50131742068A86D17958E.description: Sing with stylistic and technical accuracy, a large and varied repertoire of vocal literature, written and memorized, by oneself and in ensembles (level of difficulty: 5 on a scale of 1-6).

0325BA80DFE50131741F68A86D17958E.description: Sing in small ensembles, with one performer for each part, demonstrating effective balance, intonation, and rhythmic unity (level of difficulty: 5 on a scale of 1-6).

03252E30DFE50131741E68A86D17958E.description: Sing music written in two, three, and/or four parts with and without accompaniment.

03249D60DFE50131741D68A86D17958E.description: Sing with stylistic and technical accuracy, a large and varied repertoire of vocal literature, written and memorized (level of difficulty: 4 on a scale of 1-6).

03242F90DFE50131741C68A86D17958E.description: Sing in small ensembles demonstrating effective balance, intonation, and rhythmic unity (level of difficulty: 4 on a scale of 1-6).

03233990DFE50131741A68A86D17958E.description: Sing and perform on instruments alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

0322C6E0DFE50131741968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a given musical work in terms of its qualities and explain the musical means used to evoke feelings and emotions.

03224D30DFE50131741868A86D17958E.description: Apply and refine specific criteria for making informed critical evaluations of the quality and effectiveness of music performances, compositions, arrangements, and improvisations and apply those criteria in personal participation in music.

0321C700DFE50131741768A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a performance, composition, arrangement, or improvisation by comparing each with an exemplary model.

03205600DFE50131741468A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe the use of musical elements in a given work that makes it unique, interesting, and expressive.

031FE0E0DFE50131741368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the use of form, both past and present, in a varied repertoire of music from diverse genres, styles, and cultures.

031F5B70DFE50131741268A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe significant musical events perceived and remembered in a given aural example.

031EE250DFE50131741168A86D17958E.description: Compare ways in which musical devices are used in a given example relative to ways in which they are used in other works of the same genre or style.

031D76B0DFE50131740E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the use of forms in a varied repertoire of music representing diverse genres, styles, and cultures.

031CF460DFE50131740D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe the use of musical elements and expressive devices (e.g., articulation, dynamic markings) in aural examples of a varied repertoire of music representing diverse genres, styles, and cultures.

031C63E0DFE50131740C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain a variety of compositional devices and techniques used to provide unity, variety, tension, and release in aural examples.

031B7600DFE50131740A68A86D17958E.description: Listen to, analyze, and evaluate music.

031A98C0DFE50131740868A86D17958E.description: Research important historical dance events. Create a project that illustrates their cultural, social, political and historical significance.

0318C5B0DFE50131740468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast how choreographers use various forms, styles, and genres of dance for individual, cultural, and social expression in both the past and present.

03185640DFE50131740368A86D17958E.description: Create a dance based upon a literary work that explores the personal meaning behind the author's intent.

0317E050DFE50131740268A86D17958E.description: Create an interdisciplinary project based on a theme that includes dance and two other academic disciplines.

031773F0DFE50131740168A86D17958E.description: Create an original solo based upon a well-known work of an artist from another artistic discipline.

031701A0DFE50131740068A86D17958E.description: Interconnect - Apply dance and movement concepts to construct meaning and understanding in the arts, other subject areas, literacy, historical periods, and multiple cultures.

031689E0DFE5013173FF68A86D17958E.description: Use multiple sets of criteria for improvised and choreographed material to defend personal performances and critique the choreography and performance of others. Suggest alternative movement possibilities. Articulate responses in the form of verbal and written critical analyses.

03161030DFE5013173FE68A86D17958E.description: Critique personal dance performances and performances of others. Analyze the elements of dance, aesthetic principles, choreographic principles, and performance competencies to determine creative and artistic value.

03159C20DFE5013173FD68A86D17958E.description: Understand dance as an expression of the values and beliefs of a culture and how the protocols of dance relate to these beliefs.

03150EC0DFE5013173FC68A86D17958E.description: Observe major repertory from a variety of international dance companies.
