document.title: District of Columbia Health Education Standards

10F818E0DFE501318D7168A86D17958E.description: Apply responsible decision-making skills, including identifying and making choices and explaining the consequences of each choice.

10F78CB0DFE501318D6F68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to implement decision-making and goal-setting skills to enhance health.

10F742F0DFE501318D6E68A86D17958E.description: Describe strategies to handle and avoid fights with bullies.

10F6F980DFE501318D6D68A86D17958E.description: Summarize ways to use nonviolent strategies to resolve conflict and compromise in a manner that is fair to all persons involved.

10F67010DFE501318D6B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to show respect for others by the way one behaves, talks, and touches, including how not to interrupt or talk when someone else is talking.

10F622D0DFE501318D6A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to express concern for a friend or family member who has been hurt or has a problem.

10F5E400DFE501318D6968A86D17958E.description: Explain how failing to listen, yelling, blaming, criticizing, and/or name-calling impair communication.

10F568B0DFE501318D6768A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to utilize interpersonal communication skills to enhance and protect health.

10F52A00DFE501318D6668A86D17958E.description: Describe the positive and negative influence of the media on thoughts, feelings, perceptions, and health behaviors.

10F49EA0DFE501318D6468A86D17958E.description: Explain that individuals have different cultural backgrounds that influence dietary customs and recreational activities.

10F44690DFE501318D6368A86D17958E.description: Describe how families take care of one another and set rules to help members live together healthily.

10F3AEF0DFE501318D6168A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to analyze the influence of family, culture, media, and technology on health and health behaviors.

10F36E00DFE501318D6068A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate appropriate and safe behavior when interacting with strangers, acquaintances and trusted adults, including how to say "no" firmly, state a reason, and get help from a trusted adult.

10F32C90DFE501318D5F68A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate basic fire and water safety skills.

10F296D0DFE501318D5D68A86D17958E.description: Assess one's personal hygiene habits and determine whether there are areas needing improvement.

10F213E0DFE501318D5B68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to apply self-management skills to enhance personal health and safety.

10F1CD40DFE501318D5A68A86D17958E.description: Obtain basic information from the product safety labels of household products; and understand the effects of misusing them.

10F176E0DFE501318D5968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to seek help when feeling ill (from police, fire and emergency care personnel) and to locate resources from home, school, and the community that can provide valid health information.

10F0DB60DFE501318D5768A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to access and evaluate health information, products, and services.

10F02430DFE501318D5468A86D17958E.description: Explain how to use medicine properly (e.g., under particular circumstances and with the supervision of a trusted adult).

10EFE7B0DFE501318D5368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between legal and illegal drugs and give examples of each.

10EE0C40DFE501318D4C68A86D17958E.description: Explain why one should limit foods that are high in fats, sugars, and sodium which can lead to a variety of health problems.

10EF62C0DFE501318D5168A86D17958E.description: Explain how regular health check-ups and screening can prevent, detect, and treat health problems and why diseases and health conditions need to be detected and treated early.

10F09E00DFE501318D5668A86D17958E.description: Describe the physical differences and similarities of gender.

10EED840DFE501318D4F68A86D17958E.description: Explain that bodies change as they grow older.

10EE9730DFE501318D4E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the skeletal and muscular systems help humans move and protect parts of the body.

10ED67D0DFE501318D4A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how teasing or making fun of people with differences hurts feelings and negatively affects the social and emotional health of the school and community.

10ED1F60DFE501318D4968A86D17958E.description: Describe how people who are caring and encouraging help their friends feel good about themselves and positively impact the health of their school and community.

10EC9440DFE501318D4768A86D17958E.description: Express feelings in healthy ways in order to create positive relationships.

10EBF790DFE501318D4568A86D17958E.description: Students comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention.

document.title: District of Columbia Social Studies Standards

0F12E1B0DFE50131894D68A86D17958E.description: Students know the distinction between sound generalizations and misleading oversimplifications and stereotypes, such as the attribution of individual perspectives on historical events to entire demographic groups.

0F129BF0DFE50131894C68A86D17958E.description: Students detect the different historical points of view on historical events and determine the context in which the historical statements were made (the questions asked, sources used, and author's perspectives).

0F125340DFE50131894B68A86D17958E.description: Students assess the credibility and reliability of Internet sources.

0F120230DFE50131894A68A86D17958E.description: Students assess the credibility of primary and secondary sources, draw sound conclusions from them, and cite sources appropriately.

0F11A1B0DFE50131894968A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish relevant from irrelevant information, essential from incidental information, and verifiable from unverifiable information in historical narratives and stories.

0F1159D0DFE50131894868A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish fact from opinion in historical narratives and stories. They know facts are true statements because they are supported by reliable evidence and can cease to be facts if new evidence renders previous evidence wrong or unreliable.

0F157020DFE50131895568A86D17958E.description: Students frame questions that can be answered by historical study and research.

0F1522C0DFE50131895468A86D17958E.description: Students interpret basic indicators of economic performance, and they conduct cost-benefit analyses of economic and political issues.

0F14D590DFE50131895368A86D17958E.description: Students recognize that interpretations of history are subject to change as new information is uncovered.

0F148140DFE50131895268A86D17958E.description: Students recognize the role of chance, oversight, and error in history.

0F142AF0DFE50131895168A86D17958E.description: Students explain the sources of historical continuity and how the combination of ideas and events explains the emergence of new patterns.

0F13C830DFE50131895068A86D17958E.description: Students understand and distinguish cause, effect, sequence, and correlation in historical events, including the short-term causes or sparks from long-term causes.

0F137640DFE50131894F68A86D17958E.description: Students explain the central issues and problems from the past, placing people and events in a matrix of time and place.

0F132E00DFE50131894E68A86D17958E.description: Students construct various time lines of key events, people, and periods of the historical era they are studying.

0F111570DFE50131894768A86D17958E.description: Students explain how major events are related to one another in time.

0F0DF1B0DFE50131893D68A86D17958E.description: Students use geographic knowledge and skills to analyze historical and contemporary issues.

0F0D9510DFE50131893C68A86D17958E.description: Students apply the concept of region and their patterns of change to the study of the natural and human characteristics of places.

0F108A30DFE50131894568A86D17958E.description: Students explain the effects of interactions between humans and natural systems, including how humans depend on natural resources and adapt to and affect the natural environment.

0F103F60DFE50131894468A86D17958E.description: Students identify and explain the process of conflict and cooperation (political, economic, religious, etc.) among people in the contemporary world at local, national, regional, and international scales.

0F0FE8F0DFE50131894368A86D17958E.description: Students assess how people's changing perceptions of geographic features have led to changes in human societies. They study current events to describe how people's experiences of diverse cultures and places influences their perceptions and viewpoints.

0F0FA550DFE50131894268A86D17958E.description: Students study current events to identify the characteristics, distribution, and complexity of earth's cultural mosaics.

0F0F6090DFE50131894168A86D17958E.description: Students explain the historical migration of people, expansion and disintegration of empires, and the growth of economic systems. Identify spatial patterns in the movement of people, goods, and ideas throughout history.

0F0F1330DFE50131894068A86D17958E.description: Students categorize characteristics of places in terms of whether they are physical (natural) or cultural (human). Know and apply the subcategories of physical and cultural characteristics when describing any given place.

0F0EC6A0DFE50131893F68A86D17958E.description: Students create maps that show the growth and decline of empires.

0F0E6000DFE50131893E68A86D17958E.description: Students use a variety of maps and documents to identify physical and cultural features of neighborhoods, cities, states, and countries. Students interpret historical maps and charts.

0F0D4190DFE50131893B68A86D17958E.description: Students explain Earth's grid system and are able to locate places using degrees of latitude and longitude.

0F37DF10DFE5013189C268A86D17958E.description: Explain the connection between the ideology of Manifest Destiny and accelerated economic growth of the United States in the late 19th century (e.g., connection between U.S. business interests and military intervention in Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean). (P, E)

(G, S)

0F36E950DFE5013189BF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the location and effects of urbanization, renewed immigration, and industrialization (e.g., the effects on social fabric of cities, wealth and economic opportunity, and the conservation movement). (G, S, E)

0F2BC700DFE50131899C68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the paths of the American people in the South from 1800 to the mid-1800s and the challenges they faced.

0F29A670DFE50131899568A86D17958E.description: Outline the physical obstacles to and the economic and political factors involved in building a network of roads, canals, and railroads (e.g., Henry Clay's American System). (G, E)

0F295900DFE50131899468A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of industrialization and technological developments on the region, including human modification of the landscape and how physical geography shaped human actions (e.g., growth of cities, deforestation, farming, and mineral extraction). (G)

0F28FDC0DFE50131899368A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the states that made up the Northern region of the United States on a map. (G)

0F28AA90DFE50131899268A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the paths of the American people in the North from 1800 to the mid-1800s and the challenges they faced.

0F2613F0DFE50131898968A86D17958E.description: The Divergent and Unifying Paths of the American People (1800-1850)

0F25C680DFE50131898868A86D17958E.description: Identify on a map the changing boundaries of the United States and the relationships the country had with its neighbors (currently Mexico and Canada) and Europe, including the influence of the Monroe Doctrine, and explain how those relationships influenced westward expansion and the Mexican-American War. (G, P)

0F2573F0DFE50131898768A86D17958E.description: Outline the major treaties with American Indian nations during the administrations of the first four presidents and the varying outcomes of those treaties. (P)

0F2525E0DFE50131898668A86D17958E.description: Explain the political and economic causes and consequences of the War of 1812 and the major battles, leaders, and events that led to a final peace. (P, M, E)

0F24DD50DFE50131898568A86D17958E.description: Students analyze U.S. foreign policy in the early Republic.

0F249350DFE50131898468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the rise of capitalism and the economic problems and conflicts that accompanied it (e.g., Jackson's opposition to the National Bank; early decisions of the U.S. Supreme Court that reinforced the sanctity of contracts). (E)

0F244840DFE50131898368A86D17958E.description: Describe daily life — including traditions in art, music, and literature — of early national America (e.g., through writings by Washington Irving, and James Fenimore Cooper). (S, I)

0F23F9D0DFE50131898268A86D17958E.description: Explain and identify on a map the territorial expansion during the terms of the first four presidents (e.g., the Lewis and Clark expedition, the Louisiana Purchase). (G, P)

0F239F90DFE50131898168A86D17958E.description: Explain the policy significance of famous speeches (e.g., Washington's farewell address and Jefferson's 1801 inaugural address). (P)

0F234AB0DFE50131898068A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the aspirations and ideals of the people of the new nation.

0F229F90DFE50131897E68A86D17958E.description: Enumerate the advantages of a common market among the states as foreseen in and protected by the Constitution's clauses on interstate commerce, common coinage, etc. (E)

0F225780DFE50131897D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic law-making process and how the Constitution provides numerous opportunities for citizens to participate in the political process and to monitor and influence government (e.g., function of elections, political parties, and interest groups). (P)

0F220AC0DFE50131897C68A86D17958E.description: Understand the significance of domestic resistance movements and the way in which the central government responded to such movements (e.g., Shays' Rebellion and the Whiskey Rebellion). (P)

0F21B490DFE50131897B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the strict versus loose interpretation of the Constitution and how the conflicts between Thomas Jefferson and Alexander Hamilton resulted in the emergence of two political parties (e.g., their views of foreign policy, Alien and Sedition Acts, economic policy, National Bank, funding, and assumption of the revolutionary debt). (P)

0F216B70DFE50131897A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the ordinances of 1785 and 1787 privatized national resources and transferred federally owned lands into private holdings, townships, and states. (G, P)

0F212200DFE50131897968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the principles and concepts codified in state constitutions between 1777 and 1781 that created the context out of which American political institutions and ideas developed. (P)

0F20D6A0DFE50131897868A86D17958E.description: Students understand the foundation of the American political system and the ways in which citizens participate in it.

0F1DCD40DFE50131896F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the need and reasons for amendments to the Constitution. (P)

0F208AF0DFE50131897768A86D17958E.description: Describe the powers of government set forth in the Constitution and the fundamental liberties ensured by the Bill of Rights. (P)

0F202BA0DFE50131897668A86D17958E.description: Explain the significance of Jefferson's Statute for Religious Freedom as a forerunner of the First Amendment. (P, R)

0F1FD960DFE50131897568A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the origins, purpose, and differing views of the framers on the issue of the separation of church and state. (P, R)

0F1F9040DFE50131897468A86D17958E.description: Describe the principles of federalism, dual sovereignty, separation of powers, checks and balances, the nature and purpose of majority rule, and the ways in which the American idea of constitutionalism preserves individual rights. (P)

0F1F45B0DFE50131897368A86D17958E.description: Describe the political philosophy underpinning the Constitution as specified in The Federalist Papers (by James Madison, Alexander Hamilton, and John Jay), and explain the role of such leaders as James Madison, George Washington, Roger Sherman, Gouverneur Morris, and James Wilson in the writing and ratification of the Constitution. (P)

0F1EF240DFE50131897268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the major debates that occurred during the development of the Constitution and their ultimate resolutions in such areas as shared power among institutions, divided state-federal power, slavery, the rights of individuals and states (later addressed by the addition of the Bill of Rights), and the status of American Indian nations. (P)

0F1E6DD0DFE50131897168A86D17958E.description: Explain the Constitution and its success in implementing the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. (P)

0F1E14E0DFE50131897068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the Articles of Confederation and the reasons for its replacement by the Constitution. (P)

0F1D7D60DFE50131896E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the significance of the Magna Carta, the English Bill of Rights, and the Mayflower Compact. (P)

0F1D0CD0DFE50131896D68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the political principles underlying the U.S. Constitution, and they compare the enumerated and implied powers of the federal government.

0F1CAD00DFE50131896C68A86D17958E.description: The Constitution of the United States (1777-1789)

0F1C5700DFE50131896B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the functions and responsibilities of a free press. (P)

0F1C12D0DFE50131896A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the nation's blend of civic republicanism, classical liberal principles, and English parliamentary traditions. (P)

0F1BCE90DFE50131896968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the American Revolution influenced other nations' revolutions. (P)

0F1B8710DFE50131896868A86D17958E.description: Identify the political and economic causes and consequences of the American Revolution and the major battles, leaders, and events that led to a final peace (e.g., free press and taxation without representation). (P, M, E)

0F1B3A00DFE50131896768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the philosophy of government expressed in the Declaration of Independence, with an emphasis on government as a means of securing individual rights (e.g., key phrases such as "all men are created equal, that they are endowed by their creator with certain unalienable rights"). (P)

0F1AECE0DFE50131896668A86D17958E.description: Explain how freedom from European feudalism and aristocracy and the widespread ownership of property fostered individualism and contributed to the American Revolution. (P)

0F1A9AC0DFE50131896568A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between the moral and political ideas of the Great Awakening and the development of revolutionary fervor. (P, R)

0F1A55D0DFE50131896468A86D17958E.description: Students understand the major events preceding the founding of the nation and relate their significance to the development of American constitutional democracy.

0F16E6A0DFE50131895A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the origins and development of slavery in the colonies, the struggle between proponents and opponents of slavery in the colonies, and overt and passive resistance to enslavement (e.g., the Middle Passage). (P, S)

0F19B9C0DFE50131896268A86D17958E.description: Explain that some Africans came to America as indentured servants who were released at the end of their indentures, as well as those who came as captives to slavery. (G, E, S)

0F196490DFE50131896168A86D17958E.description: Examine the beginnings of Africans in America by identifying some of the major ethnic/national groups that came (e.g., Yoruba, Ibo, Bambara, Ki-Kongo, Wolof, Akan, and Hausas).

0F18FFA0DFE50131896068A86D17958E.description: Describe the day-to-day colonial life for men, women, and children in different regions and their connection to the land. (S, E)

0F18ADC0DFE50131895F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the significance and leaders of the First Great Awakening, which marked a shift in religious ideas, practices, and allegiances in the colonial period and the growth in religious toleration and free exercise of religion. (R)

0F1814C0DFE50131895D68A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the first 13 colonies, and describe how their location and natural environment influenced their development. (G)

0F17BC60DFE50131895C68A86D17958E.description: Explain geographic reasons for the development of communications and smuggling within the colonies (irregular coastlines, need for products not produced locally). (G)

0F174700DFE50131895B68A86D17958E.description: Explain instances of both cooperation and conflict between Native Americans and European settlers, such as agriculture, trade, cultural exchanges, and military alliances, as well as later broken treaties, massacres, and conflicts over control of the land. 0F169FB0DFE50131895968A86D17958E.description: Describe the varied economies and trade networks within and among major indigenous cultures prior to contact with Europeans and their systems of government, religious beliefs, distinct territories, and customs and traditions. (G, P, R, E)

0F165610DFE50131895868A86D17958E.description: Students explain the religious, political, and economic reasons for movement of people from Europe to the Americas, and they describe the impact of exploration and settlement by Europeans on Native Americans.

0F15BF80DFE50131895668A86D17958E.description: U.S. History and Geography I: Growth and Conflict

document.title: District of Columbia Science Standards

0B9D8B90DFE5013183B268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe how artifacts and preserved remains provide some evidence of the physical characteristics and possible behaviors of human beings and their ancestors who lived long ago.

0B9FDAE0DFE5013183BA68A86D17958E.description: Examine the information that fossils provide us about living things that inhabited the Earth in the distant past, and describe how they can be compared both to one another and to living organisms according to their similarities and differences.

0B9F83D0DFE5013183B968A86D17958E.description: Describe well-defined plant behaviors, such as the way seedlings' stems grow toward light and their roots grow downward in response to gravity.

0B9F3A50DFE5013183B868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that some animal behaviors are instinctive (e.g., turtles burying their eggs, human infants crying when hungry) and others learned (e.g., a wolf's hunting skills, humans' ability to build fires for warmth).

0B9EED90DFE5013183B768A86D17958E.description: Explain that many plants and animals can survive harsh environments because of seasonal behaviors (e.g., in winter, some trees shed leaves, some animals hibernate).

0B9EA820DFE5013183B668A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in an organism's habitat are sometimes beneficial and sometimes harmful, and how changes in the environment (drought, cold) have caused some plants and animals to die, migrate, or become extinct.

0B9E6480DFE5013183B568A86D17958E.description: Explain that organisms fit enough to survive in a particular environment will typically produce offspring fit enough to survive and reproduce in that particular environment. Over time, these inherited characteristics are carried as the predominant forms (e.g., adaptations such as shape of beak, length of neck, shape of teeth).

0B9E1BE0DFE5013183B468A86D17958E.description: Explain how organisms can cause changes in their environment to ensure survival, and these changes may affect the ecosystem (the living and nonliving components of the environment).

0B9DD050DFE5013183B368A86D17958E.description: Identify organisms that are not native to the Washington, DC, area and how they undergo changes to increase their chance of survival in the area.

0B9D3AE0DFE5013183B168A86D17958E.description: Explain that in any particular environment, some kinds of plants and animals survive well, some do not survive as well, and some cannot survive at all.

0B9CF150DFE5013183B068A86D17958E.description: Adaptations in physical structure or behavior may improve an organism's chance for survival. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B9C9B80DFE5013183AF68A86D17958E.description: List some characteristics of plants and animals that are fully inherited (e.g., form of flower, shape of leaves) and others that are affected by the climate or environmental conditions (e.g., browning of leaves from too much sun, language spoken).

0B9C5000DFE5013183AE68A86D17958E.description: Explain why there must be a reliable way to transfer information from one generation to the next in order for offspring to resemble their parents.

0B9BF030DFE5013183AD68A86D17958E.description: Many characteristics of an organism are inherited from the parents, but others result from the influence of the environment. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B9BA5E0DFE5013183AC68A86D17958E.description: Explain that in complex organisms such as humans, cells can have a very wide variety of forms and perform very different roles (e.g., nerve cells, muscle cells, and fat cells).

0B9B6130DFE5013183AB68A86D17958E.description: Observe and explain that some organisms are made of a collection of similar cells that benefit from cooperating.

0B9B1C80DFE5013183AA68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe that some organisms consist of a single cell that needs an environment that can supply food, water, sometimes oxygen, and a way to dispose of waste. (Some single-celled organisms are anaerobes.)

0B9AD310DFE5013183A968A86D17958E.description: All living things are composed of cells, from just one to many quadrillions, whose details usually are visible only through a microscope. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B9A23F0DFE5013183A768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and explain that things on or near Earth are pulled toward Earth's center by the gravitational force that Earth exerts on them.

0B99D230DFE5013183A668A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that the greater the net force, F, applied to a body, the greater its acceleration, a. Describe that the greater the mass, m, of an object, the smaller the acceleration produced by a given force.

0B997E20DFE5013183A568A86D17958E.description: Describe that, for an object moving in a straight line, acceleration, a, is the change in velocity, v, divided by the time, t, that change takes (a = v ÷ t).

0B993B10DFE5013183A468A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that unbalanced forces cause changes in the speed and/or direction of motion of an object (acceleration).

0B98F680DFE5013183A368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate that if the forces acting on an object are balanced so that the net force is zero, the object will remain at rest if it is initially at rest or will maintain a constant speed and direction if it is initially moving.

0B98AEF0DFE5013183A268A86D17958E.description: Explain that objects can move with a very wide range of speeds, with some moving very slowly and some moving too quickly for people to see them.

0B985DD0DFE5013183A168A86D17958E.description: Unbalanced forces cause changes in velocity. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B9819E0DFE5013183A068A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe how some materials conduct heat much better than others, and poor conductors (insulators) can be used to reduce heat loss or gain.

0B97D2D0DFE50131839F68A86D17958E.description: Explain that when a warm object and a cool one are placed in contact, heat flows from the warmer object to the cooler one until they are both at the same temperature. Know that heat transfer can also occur at a distance by radiation.

0B977B80DFE50131839E68A86D17958E.description: Explain that many kinds of chemical changes occur faster at higher temperatures.

0B971080DFE50131839D68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that heating and cooling cause changes in the properties of substances. For example, liquid water can turn into steam by boiling, and liquid water can turn into ice by freezing.

0B96C530DFE50131839C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that all matter is made up of an element, a compound, or mixtures of elements and compounds.

0B967B40DFE50131839B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there are more than 100 different kinds of atoms (each called an element), which are displayed on the periodic table of the elements.

0B9637C0DFE50131839A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all matter is made of small particles called atoms, which are too small to see with our eyes; describe how atoms may combine to form molecules or crystalline solids (compounds).

0B95F280DFE50131839968A86D17958E.description: Energy and matter have multiple forms and can be changed from one form to another. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B9568B0DFE50131839768A86D17958E.description: Using maps and globes, recognize that the Earth's oceans are all connected as one body of water that covers about three-quarters of the Earth's surface.

0B951D90DFE50131839668A86D17958E.description: Explain that water on Earth cycles through different forms and in different locations (e.g., underground water and vapor in the atmosphere).

0B94CEF0DFE50131839568A86D17958E.description: Explain how global patterns, such as the jet stream and ocean currents, influence local weather and climate in ways that can be measured in terms of temperature, pressure, wind direction and speed, and amounts of precipitation.

0B9487B0DFE50131839468A86D17958E.description: Describe that winds blow from areas of higher pressure to areas of lower pressure.

0B943B00DFE50131839368A86D17958E.description: Explain that the air around us is matter and has weight (a force) and exerts pressure; explain that air pressure varies a little from place to place and from time to time.

0B93FB60DFE50131839268A86D17958E.description: Describe that clouds are made of tiny droplets of water or ice crystals.

0B93BA00DFE50131839168A86D17958E.description: Explain how water moves in air masses from one place to another in the form of clouds, fog, or as invisible water vapor, and falls to the Earth as rain, hail, sleet, or snow.

0B9376C0DFE50131839068A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that when liquid water evaporates, it turns into a gas (vapor) mixed into the air, and can condense and reappear as a liquid when cooled or as a solid (ice) if cooled below the freezing point of water.

0B932610DFE50131838F68A86D17958E.description: Water on Earth moves from the ocean to the land through the processes of evaporation and condensation. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B92D640DFE50131838E68A86D17958E.description: Observe stars and identify ones that are unusually bright, and others that have unusual colors, such as red or blue.

0B9288E0DFE50131838D68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe that stars vary in size, but they are so far away that they look like points of light.

0B923810DFE50131838C68A86D17958E.description: Observe how telescopes are used both to magnify images of distant objects in the sky, including the moon and the planets, and to gather enough light from very dim objects to make them visible.

0B91E1A0DFE50131838B68A86D17958E.description: Explain that the alternation between day and night and the apparent movement of the sun, moon, and stars across the sky depend on the rotation of the Earth on its axis.

0B917C50DFE50131838A68A86D17958E.description: Describe that, like all planets and stars, the Earth is approximately spherical in shape.

0B9123D0DFE50131838968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how the Earth orbits the sun in a year's time, and Earth rotates on its axis about once every 24 hours.

0B90E0F0DFE50131838868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the Earth is the third planet from the sun in our solar system.

0B909EA0DFE50131838768A86D17958E.description: Describe the Earth as part of a system called the solar system, which includes the sun (a star), planets, comets, asteroids, and many moons.

0B905B10DFE50131838668A86D17958E.description: The solar system consists of planets and other bodies that orbit the sun in predictable paths. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0BA145E0DFE5013183BF68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of materials not present in nature that have become available because of science and technology, such as cloth, metal alloys, plastic, ceramics, and concrete.

0BA0FF30DFE5013183BE68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of advances in technology that have positively and/or negatively affected society.

0BA0B6E0DFE5013183BD68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of technology, such as telescopes, microscopes, and cameras, that enable scientists and others to observe things that are too small or too far away to be seen without them and to study the motion of objects that are moving very rapidly or are hardly moving.

0BA071D0DFE5013183BC68A86D17958E.description: Although each of the human enterprises of science and technology has a character and history of its own, each is dependent on and reinforces the other. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B8DB080DFE50131837C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the distortion inherent in using only a portion of the data collected to describe the whole. Understand that it is sometimes acceptable to discard data.

0B8D6AA0DFE50131837B68A86D17958E.description: Understand how plotting data on a number line helps in seeing where the data lie, including the outliers.

0B8FD150DFE50131838468A86D17958E.description: Determine area and volume of rectangular shapes from linear dimensions, using the expressions A = l x w and V = l x w x h.

0B8F8250DFE50131838368A86D17958E.description: Realize and explain why predictions may be more accurate if they are based on large collections of similar events for statistical accuracy.

0B8F42A0DFE50131838268A86D17958E.description: Explain that predictions can be based on what is known about the past, assuming that conditions are similar.

0B8F0450DFE50131838168A86D17958E.description: Identify the controlled variable and at least one independent variable in a scientific investigation, when appropriate.

0B8EC610DFE50131838068A86D17958E.description: Read and follow step-by-step instructions when learning new investigations.

0B8E85D0DFE50131837F68A86D17958E.description: Write instructions that others can follow to carry out an investigation.

0B8E4460DFE50131837E68A86D17958E.description: Keep a notebook to record observations and be able to distinguish inferences from actual observations.

0B8DFDF0DFE50131837D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the validity of claims based on the amount and quality of the evidence cited.

0B8D0200DFE50131837A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe how results of similar scientific investigations may turn out differently because of inconsistencies in methods, materials, and observations, or because of limitations of the precision of the instruments used.

0B8C95F0DFE50131837968A86D17958E.description: Scientific progress is made by asking relevant questions and conducting careful investigations. As a basis for understanding this concept, and to address the content in this grade, students should develop their own questions and perform investigations. Students:

document.title: District of Columbia Arts Education Learning Standards

00680F10DFE50131702F68A86D17958E.description: Access a variety of resources such as books, a CD-ROM or visit a museum website to research an artist or art movement; share new information with classmates, e.g. National Gallery of Art: www.nga.gov; The Metropolitan Museum of Art's Timeline of Art History: www.metmuseum.org/toah; Art Institute of Chicago: www.artic.edu/aic/collections/index.php.

0067AA90DFE50131702E68A86D17958E.description: Establish criteria to use in selecting works of art for a specific type of art exhibition.

0066D230DFE50131702C68A86D17958E.description: Describe tactics employed in advertising to sway the viewer's thinking and provide examples.

0065F790DFE50131702A68A86D17958E.description: Create a tessellation showing a translation, reflection or rotation. Distinguish the three types.

006585C0DFE50131702968A86D17958E.description: Create a line design using a variety of angles, triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons. Identify the lines and shapes used.

00651A70DFE50131702868A86D17958E.description: Write and illustrate a journal using the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, editing/proofreading, publishing/presenting).

0064B190DFE50131702768A86D17958E.description: Write a poem or story inspired by original works of art.

00644B70DFE50131702668A86D17958E.description: Research how traditional characters (such as the trickster) found in a variety of cultures past and present are represented in illustrations.

00637B80DFE50131702468A86D17958E.description: Connect and apply what is learned in the visual arts to other art forms, subject areas, visual culture and communications and to careers. (Connections, Relationships, Applications)

00631360DFE50131702368A86D17958E.description: Articulate reasons for changing, editing, or revising personal works of art after a critique and museum visit.

0062B0B0DFE50131702268A86D17958E.description: Develop specific criteria alone or in groups to assess and critique works of art.

006247E0DFE50131702168A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe ways in which culture is reflected in current works of art.

0061D4A0DFE50131702068A86D17958E.description: Judge own work against a rubric. Discuss what he/she liked about the work and what he/she did not like about the work, in writing, using appropriate visual and qualitative (aesthetic) vocabulary.

00615800DFE50131701F68A86D17958E.description:
Construct and describe interpretations of what is perceived in works of art using aesthetic valuing vocabulary - the subject (the image viewers can identify), the composition (the way the principles of design are used to organize the elements of design), and content (the message the work communicates):
  • Subject
  • Composition
  • Content
  • Description
  • Significance
  • Merit

00608CE0DFE50131701D68A86D17958E.description: Respond to, analyze, and make judgments about works in the visual arts. (Aesthetics, Valuing & Perspectives of Art)

00601B30DFE50131701C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of religious groups' history on art and architecture, focusing primarily on buildings in the District of Columbia both past and present.

005F9310DFE50131701B68A86D17958E.description: Compare, in oral or written form, representative images or designs from at least two selected cultures, to identify universal symbols and themes, based on museum internet research or a museum visit.

005F3470DFE50131701A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a fundamental awareness of architectural styles and the ways that these have influenced painting and sculpture.

005ED2F0DFE50131701968A86D17958E.description: Describe how selected works of art from ethnic groups in selected world regions and countries have changed or not changed in theme and content over a period of time.

005E6A50DFE50131701868A86D17958E.description: Describe the function and meaning of specific works of art and objects from Asia.

005DFFA0DFE50131701768A86D17958E.description: Describe the various ways that ethnic groups in the U.S., world regions and countries, understand and value art and design.

005D9840DFE50131701668A86D17958E.description: Identify the characteristics and purposes of works of world art in historical and cultural contexts.

005D32A0DFE50131701568A86D17958E.description: Historical Development, Role and Cultural Diversity of the Visual Arts

005CC380DFE50131701468A86D17958E.description: Investigate and understand historical and cultural dimensions of the visual arts and to construct meaning in the diverse ways in which human experience is expressed across time and place. (Historical and Cultural Context)

005C4E50DFE50131701368A86D17958E.description: Use contemporary technology to create original works of art (e.g., color and texture methods on computers, fonts/point systems, animation techniques, video teleconferencing, multimedia techniques).

005BDE70DFE50131701268A86D17958E.description: Design and create an expressive figurative sculpture.

005B7910DFE50131701168A86D17958E.description: Select specific media and processes to express moods, feelings, themes, or ideas.

005B11E0DFE50131701068A86D17958E.description: Expression Through Original Works of Art

005A9E50DFE50131700F68A86D17958E.description: Maintain the workspace, materials, and tools responsibly and safely.

005A24D0DFE50131700E68A86D17958E.description: Use varying values of tints, shades, and intensities when drawing(e.g. portraits, still life, landscapes) to define form

0059BE40DFE50131700D68A86D17958E.description: Use curved lines to create a symmetrical and/or asymmetrical drawing using implied and overlapping lines.

00595490DFE50131700C68A86D17958E.description: Apply the rules of one-point perspective in creating a thematic work of art (e.g. landscape)

005867E0DFE50131700A68A86D17958E.description: Apply artistic processes and skills in a variety of media to communicate meaning and intent in original works of art. (Production and Creative Expression)

0057E5B0DFE50131700968A86D17958E.description: Recognize contemporary technology in works of art (e.g., color fills on computers, texture methods on computers, fonts/point systems, animation techniques, video teleconferencing, multimedia techniques). View artists examples, e.g., Nam June Paik, video artist, (SAAM); Hayao Miyazaki, animated filmmaker.

005773C0DFE50131700868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe examples of art that shapes the natural environment (e.g. gardens, eco-design, etc.).

0056F860DFE50131700768A86D17958E.description: Visit museum /gallery to study figurative sculpture, (e.g. Northwest Native American masks, Tlingit, Kwakiutl, Yup'ik Eskimo, National Museum of the American Indian).

00569230DFE50131700668A86D17958E.description: Visit a museum to identify examples of balance through symmetry, (e.g. Henri Matisse, Large Composition with Masks (National Gallery of Art), Eiffel Tower, Brooklyn Bridge, Islamic tilework; M.C. Escher; and asymmetry, e.g. Chinese landscapes (Freer/Sackler), Edgar Degas, Four Dancers (NGA*)

00562FF0DFE50131700568A86D17958E.description: Describe how balance is effectively used in work of art (e.g., symmetrical, asymmetrical, radial).

0055CB90DFE50131700468A86D17958E.description: Identify one point perspective and how artists use value, light and shadow to show emphasis in perspective drawings.

00556130DFE50131700368A86D17958E.description: Describe the differences between two and three-dimensional visual fields.

0054E8C0DFE50131700268A86D17958E.description: Identify and discuss works of art including the subject, theme, genre, style, function, and differences in media. Describe how an artist can use the same theme in a work of art using different media and style resulting in a different effect.

00548170DFE50131700168A86D17958E.description: Discuss the technique of implied line, value contrasts, and variations of value to provide shape identification and visual separation of objects.

00541D60DFE50131700068A86D17958E.description: Develop a working understanding of line drawing techniques. Interpret the technical characteristics of a drawing such as the convexity, specificity, technical qualities, and axis.

0053BD70DFE501316FFF68A86D17958E.description: Develop perceptual skills, analyze elements of art and the principles of design

005356D0DFE501316FFE68A86D17958E.description: Perceive and understand the components of visual language: the elements of art and the principles of design. (Artistic Perception)

00528B60DFE501316FFC68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast how works of theatre from different cultures or time periods convey the same or similar content or plot.

00522A60DFE501316FFB68A86D17958E.description: Use theatrical skills to identify and communicate rhetorical ideas from other curriculum areas (e.g., demonstration on persuasion and propaganda in advertising).

0051C600DFE501316FFA68A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of how theatre, television, and film can influence or be influenced by society, politics, and culture.

00515A40DFE501316FF968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between and among the techniques used in theatre, television, and radio.

0050ECB0DFE501316FF868A86D17958E.description: Apply theatrical concepts to construct meaning and understanding in other subject areas.

00507E40DFE501316FF768A86D17958E.description: Develop criteria and write a formal review of a theatrical performance, using basic theatre terminology.

004FFC30DFE501316FF668A86D17958E.description: Explain how a dramatic performance on video or film depicts a feeling or event the student may have experienced.

004F83F0DFE501316FF568A86D17958E.description: Identify dramatic elements within a script, such as foreshadowing, crisis, rising action, catharsis, and denouement, using the vocabulary of theatre.

004EEB80DFE501316FF468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the use of figurative language and imagery to create tone and mood in dramatic texts.

004E89F0DFE501316FF368A86D17958E.description: Use the vocabulary of theatre, such as action/reaction, vocal projection, subtext, theme, mood, design, production values and stage crew, to describe theatrical experiences.

004E2630DFE501316FF268A86D17958E.description: Analyze, critique, and respond to theatre and dramatic media.

004DC630DFE501316FF168A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of theatre technology and equipment, including various sound, lighting, and special effects systems.

004D61D0DFE501316FF068A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of sets, lights, costumes and sound in communicating dramatic elements to an audience.

004CFCE0DFE501316FEF68A86D17958E.description: Research and create appropriate props, sets, and costumes for a cultural celebration or pageant.

004C9880DFE501316FEE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a selected scene for technical and design requirements.

004C36B0DFE501316FED68A86D17958E.description: Design and manage theatrical environments for formal and informal dramatizations.

004BCB00DFE501316FEC68A86D17958E.description: Create scripts that reflect particular historical periods or cultures.

004B5C60DFE501316FEB68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of vocal expressions, gestures, facial expressions, and timing to create a range of characters.

004AE4F0DFE501316FEA68A86D17958E.description: Make acting choices when improvising in a manner that demonstrates an understanding of text, subtext, and context.

004A7310DFE501316FE968A86D17958E.description: Write, improvise, and evaluate scenes that reveal character motivation, demonstrate conflict, and advance action

004A0D20DFE501316FE868A86D17958E.description: Perform and participate in theatre improvisations and dramatizations to learn acting and scriptwriting fundamentals.

00493650DFE501316FE668A86D17958E.description: Associate aural examples of music to a variety of cultures, styles, and historical periods.

00485370DFE501316FE468A86D17958E.description: Research career and vocational options in music using available technology.

0047E430DFE501316FE368A86D17958E.description: Analyze concepts common to music and other disciplines.

0046B1D0DFE501316FE068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast materials being studied in its historical and cultural context, including music from the 20th and/or 21st century.

0045CAA0DFE501316FDE68A86D17958E.description: Research career and vocational options in music using available technology.

004558E0DFE501316FDD68A86D17958E.description: Discuss relationships between music concepts and other disciplines.

00441500DFE501316FDA68A86D17958E.description: Describe distinguishing characteristics of representative choral music from a variety of cultures.

004388F0DFE501316FD968A86D17958E.description: Classify an exemplary vocal/choral work by music style.

0042A180DFE501316FD768A86D17958E.description: Explore careers in music and relate them to careers in the other fine and performing arts.

00423C10DFE501316FD668A86D17958E.description: Examine and evaluate characteristics of various arts from a particular historic period and various cultures, using appropriate terms.

00410770DFE501316FD368A86D17958E.description: Associate distinguishing characteristics of representative choral music from a variety of cultures.

00408410DFE501316FD268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the functions of vocal/choral music in various cultures.

003FAE80DFE501316FD068A86D17958E.description: Explore careers in music and relate them to careers in the other fine and performing arts.

003F4510DFE501316FCF68A86D17958E.description: Associate common music elements and descriptive terms with those used in art, dance, and drama.

003DFCB0DFE501316FCC68A86D17958E.description: Connect music to other art forms and subject areas through understanding the historical and cultural context of music.

003BF4B0DFE501316FC768A86D17958E.description: Read and notate rhythmic and melodic notation.

003444C0DFE501316FB568A86D17958E.description: Compose rhythmically interesting melodies within specified guidelines.
