FFA92910DFE401316E7468A86D17958E.description: Listen to, analyze, and evaluate music.

FFA84AF0DFE401316E7268A86D17958E.description: Analyze dances from different cultures or historical periods in relation to the values and beliefs of their society.

FFA7E680DFE401316E7168A86D17958E.description: Create and perform a dance based upon personal original writing.

FFA78230DFE401316E7068A86D17958E.description: Identify and use different resources from other academic disciplines (such as newspapers, history books, maps, poetry) to generate ideas for dance compositions.

FFA71B00DFE401316E6F68A86D17958E.description: Use concepts from other art forms to choreograph dance studies (e.g. asymmetrical design, contrapuntal rhythm, and character development).

FFA6B420DFE401316E6E68A86D17958E.description: Interconnect - Apply dance and movement concepts to construct meaning and understanding in the arts, other subject areas, literacy, historical periods, and multiple cultures.

FFA63F60DFE401316E6D68A86D17958E.description: Identify and formulate criteria to assess the quality of a dance performance (e.g. originality of movement, technical skill, coherence, visual or emotional impact). Either orally or in writing, critique personal performances and performances of others.

FFA5D850DFE401316E6C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of the elements of dance and the principles of choreography to respond verbally or in writing to an observed dance performance.

FFA56530DFE401316E6B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of dance protocols in the dance class, rehearsal, and performance.

FFA4ED50DFE401316E6A68A86D17958E.description: Observe dances of several famous companies and, either orally or in writing, compare their dance styles and ideas. Identify and support personal preferences for dances observed using dance terminology.

FFA45DC0DFE401316E6968A86D17958E.description: Respond - Analyze, critique, and respond to dance.

FFA3F5C0DFE401316E6868A86D17958E.description: Perform a group dance developing cooperative relationships with others as follower, leader, soloist, group participant.

FFA38D20DFE401316E6768A86D17958E.description: Remember, perform, reflect, and revise choreographed dances. Demonstrate focused concentration, kinesthetic awareness, and responsibility for one's role in a dance and the production.

FFA32990DFE401316E6668A86D17958E.description: Identify major bones, muscles and joints in anatomical terminology. Understand how they function to create efficient movement, balance, flexibility, coordination, and physical control.

FFA2C200DFE401316E6568A86D17958E.description: Perform a group dance that uses variations of dynamics (energy) to reflect the ideas, feelings, images, and meaning of the dance.

FFA25760DFE401316E6468A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance that reflects the phrasing, structure, tone, and dynamic of its accompanying music.

FFA1F4F0DFE401316E6368A86D17958E.description: Perform a group dance that uses space inventively with great variations of facings, levels, directions, pathways, and shapes.

FFA191E0DFE401316E6268A86D17958E.description: Perform a dance and demonstrate physical control, alignment, balance, and coordination in performing locomotor and axial movements from a chosen dance genre (e.g. ballet, modern dance, jazz).

FFA11550DFE401316E6168A86D17958E.description: Perform - Demonstrate dance fundamentals and skills with technical proficiency and spatial, musical, and kinesthetic awareness.

FFA090C0DFE401316E6068A86D17958E.description: Research a topic of interest. Create a short dance that communicates the meaning of the research. Receive response, and revise the choreography to perform and communicate more clearly.

FFA02F10DFE401316E5F68A86D17958E.description: Create, perform, reflect, and revise a short dance using a theme that communicates a feeling or idea.

FF9FC9E0DFE401316E5E68A86D17958E.description: Create dance studies using common choreographic forms (such as narrative, theme and variation, ABA, canon, and call-and-response).

FF9F6260DFE401316E5D68A86D17958E.description: Create - Understand and create choreographic forms and meaning in dance.

document.title: District of Columbia Social Studies Standards

0E2DD8B0DFE50131876168A86D17958E.description: Students use nontext primary and secondary sources, such as maps, charts, graphs, photographs, works of art, and technical charts.

0E2D9930DFE50131876068A86D17958E.description: Students pose relevant questions about events they encounter in historical documents, eyewitness accounts, oral histories, letters, diaries, artifacts, photographs, maps, artworks, and architecture.

0E2D5780DFE50131875F68A86D17958E.description: Students differentiate between primary and secondary sources and know examples of each.

0E2D0E70DFE50131875E68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze societies in terms of the following themes: military, political, economic, social, religious, and intellectual.

0E2CB310DFE50131875D68A86D17958E.description: Historical Research, Evidence, and Point of View

0E2C6410DFE50131875C68A86D17958E.description: Students identify and explain the process of conflict and cooperation (political, economic, religious, etc.) among people in the contemporary world at local, regional, and national levels.

0E2C07F0DFE50131875B68A86D17958E.description: Students explain the causes and effects of settlement patterns, including the effect of rural-to-urban migrations.

0E2BC8C0DFE50131875A68A86D17958E.description: Students trace how changes in technology, transportation, communication, and resources affect the location of economic activities.

0E2B87D0DFE50131875968A86D17958E.description: Students describe the factors that influence the location, distribution, and interrelationships of economic activities in different regions.

0E2B4110DFE50131875868A86D17958E.description: Students explain the distributions of cultures in places they study and how they create a cultural landscape.

0E2AF380DFE50131875768A86D17958E.description: Students identify the human and physical characteristics of the places they are studying, and they explain how those features form the unique character of those places.

0E2AB140DFE50131875668A86D17958E.description: Students judge the significance of the relative location of a place (e.g., proximity to a harbor, on trade routes), and they analyze how relative advantages or disadvantages can change over time.

0E2A6CF0DFE50131875568A86D17958E.description: Students define common map and globe terms, including continent, country, mountain, valley, ocean, sea, lake, river; cardinal directions, latitude, longitude, north pole, south pole, tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, equator, 360-degree divisions, time zones; elevation, depth, approximate distances in miles, isthmus, strait, peninsula, island, archipelago, 23-and-a-half-degree global tilt, fall line; and compass rose, scale, and legend.

0E2A1170DFE50131875468A86D17958E.description: Students use map and globe skills to determine the absolute locations (latitude and longitude) of places, and they interpret information available through a map or globe's legend, scale, and symbolic representations.

0E297FA0DFE50131875268A86D17958E.description: Students conduct cost-benefit analyses of historical and current events.

0E293020DFE50131875168A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish cause from effect and identify and interpret the multiple causes and effects of historical events.

0E28F2B0DFE50131875068A86D17958E.description: Students summarize the key events of the era they are studying and explain the historical contexts of those events.

0E28B420DFE50131874F68A86D17958E.description: Students explain how the present is connected to the past, identifying both similarities and differences between the two, and how some things change over time and some things stay the same.

0E286F20DFE50131874E68A86D17958E.description: Students know the calendar abbreviations and what they signify (e.g., A.D. and C.E., B.E. and B.C.E., c. and circa).

0E282AF0DFE50131874D68A86D17958E.description: Students place key events of the historical era they are studying and interpret information contained within time lines and comparative time charts.

0E279AA0DFE50131874B68A86D17958E.description: Historical and Social Sciences Analysis Skills

0E36B6F0DFE50131878068A86D17958E.description: Students draw from historical and community resources to organize the sequence of local historical events and describe how each period of settlement left its mark on the land. (G, P)

0E366760DFE50131877F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and research outstanding statements of moral and civic principles made in Washington, DC, as well as the leaders who delivered them, that contributed to the struggle to extend equal rights to all Americans (e.g., Lincoln and his second inaugural address, Frederick Douglass and his speech against lynching at the Metropolitan AME Church, Martin Luther King Jr. and his speeches at the Lincoln Memorial in 1957 and 1963, and Rodolfo "Corky" Gonzales at the Poor People's March). (P)

0E361110DFE50131877E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how Washington, DC, was selected and named as our capital city. (P,S)

0E35A660DFE50131877D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the unique nature of Washington, DC, as the nation's capital, a multicultural urban city, and the jurisdiction that provides the state and local government for its residents. (P, S)

0E355480DFE50131877C68A86D17958E.description: Construct a chronological explanation of key people and events that were important in shaping the character of Washington, DC, during the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries. (H, P, S)

0E3515A0DFE50131877B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast how people in the past met their needs in different ways (e.g., hunting and gathering, subsistence agriculture, barter, commerce, and manufacturing). (E)

0E34D740DFE50131877A68A86D17958E.description: Emphasizing the most significant differences, students describe Washington, DC, at the end of the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries.

0E3458A0DFE50131877868A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which Washington, DC, meets the economic needs of its citizens (e.g., housing, jobs, health, transportation, and recreation). (E, S)

0E340D40DFE50131877768A86D17958E.description: Define what bartering is (e.g., trading baseball cards with each other) and how money makes it easier for people to get things they want. (E)

0E33C800DFE50131877668A86D17958E.description: Describe the specialization in jobs and businesses and provide examples of specialized businesses in the community. (E)

0E338420DFE50131877568A86D17958E.description: Explain what a tax is and the purposes for taxes, and with the help of their teachers and parents, provide examples of different kinds of taxes (e.g., property, sales, and income taxes). (E)

0E334400DFE50131877468A86D17958E.description: Outline the ways in which local producers have used and are using natural resources, human resources, and capital resources to produce goods and services in the past and the present. (G, E)

0E330500DFE50131877368A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate basic economic reasoning skills and an understanding of the economy of the local region.

0E327C70DFE50131877168A86D17958E.description: Identify the representative leaders in Washington, DC, and neighboring states. (P)

0E323110DFE50131877068A86D17958E.description: Describe the distinctions between local, state, and national government. (P)

0E31EA30DFE50131876F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the different ways people in a community can influence their local government (e.g., by voting, running for office, testifying at hearings, or participating in meetings).

0E31A220DFE50131876E68A86D17958E.description: Explain why it is necessary for communities to have governments (e.g., governments provide order and protect rights). (P)

0E315380DFE50131876D68A86D17958E.description: Describe its duties, organizational structures, and functions. (P)

0E310CE0DFE50131876C68A86D17958E.description: Students understand the basic structure of the Washington, DC, government.

0E307C00DFE50131876A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how people depend on the physical environment and its natural resources to satisfy their basic needs. (G, S)

0E303640DFE50131876968A86D17958E.description: Describe the ways in which people have used and modified resources in the local region (e.g., building roads, bridges, and cities, and raising crops). (G, S)

0E2FD590DFE50131876868A86D17958E.description: Describe the various types of communities within the city (e.g., Chinatown, Foggy Bottom, Adams Morgan, Anacostia, and Georgetown), beginning with the community in which the elementary school is located. (G, S)

0E2F7740DFE50131876768A86D17958E.description: Identify and locate major monuments and historical sites in and around Washington, DC (e.g., the Jefferson and Lincoln memorials, Smithsonian museums, Library of Congress, White House, Capitol, Washington Monument, National Archives, Arlington National Cemetery, African American Civil War Museum, Anacostia Museum, Vietnam Veterans Memorial, Iwo Jima Memorial, Frederick Douglass House, Mary McCleod Bethune House, Wilson Building, and Mount Vernon). (G, P)

0E2F34C0DFE50131876668A86D17958E.description: Identify and locate major physical features and natural characteristics (e.g., bodies of water, land forms, natural resources, and weather) in Washington, DC. (G)

0E2EEF80DFE50131876568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the differences between a contemporary map of Washington, DC, and maps of this area at the end of the 18th and 19th centuries. (G)

0E2E9460DFE50131876468A86D17958E.description: Students use cardinal directions, map scales, legends, and titles to locate places on contemporary maps of Washington, DC, and the local community.

0E2E17E0DFE50131876268A86D17958E.description: Geography and History of the District of Columbia

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

07466E80DFE501317BF468A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

0745FEB0DFE501317BF368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

07459FB0DFE501317BF268A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

07454990DFE501317BF168A86D17958E.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

07450340DFE501317BF068A86D17958E.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

0744BB80DFE501317BEF68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

07447260DFE501317BEE68A86D17958E.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

074428A0DFE501317BED68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

0743DA10DFE501317BEC68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

074375D0DFE501317BEB68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

0741FBA0DFE501317BE768A86D17958E.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

0741AA60DFE501317BE668A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

07416340DFE501317BE568A86D17958E.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

0740CD80DFE501317BE368A86D17958E.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

07406190DFE501317BE268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

073FFD10DFE501317BE168A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

073FB330DFE501317BE068A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

073F1EC0DFE501317BDE68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

073E7C60DFE501317BDC68A86D17958E.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

073E33E0DFE501317BDB68A86D17958E.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).

073DEAD0DFE501317BDA68A86D17958E.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

073DA2F0DFE501317BD968A86D17958E.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

073D4E30DFE501317BD868A86D17958E.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

073CF9A0DFE501317BD768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

073BFDB0DFE501317BD468A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

073BB1B0DFE501317BD368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

073B6200DFE501317BD268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

073AA3B0DFE501317BD068A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

073A0190DFE501317BCE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

0739B6E0DFE501317BCD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

07391080DFE501317BCB68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

0738C240DFE501317BCA68A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

07386C40DFE501317BC968A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

073818D0DFE501317BC868A86D17958E.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

07375C30DFE501317BC668A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

07371370DFE501317BC568A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

0736CCE0DFE501317BC468A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

073685F0DFE501317BC368A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

07363CC0DFE501317BC268A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

0735EEC0DFE501317BC168A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups

0734DD80DFE501317BBE68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

07348050DFE501317BBD68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

073435E0DFE501317BBC68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

073392F0DFE501317BBA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

073345A0DFE501317BB968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

0732DF90DFE501317BB868A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

07323990DFE501317BB668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

073104C0DFE501317BB268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

0730A900DFE501317BB168A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

07304E80DFE501317BB068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

072FF300DFE501317BAF68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

072FA920DFE501317BAE68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

072EBF30DFE501317BAB68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

072E6DD0DFE501317BAA68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

072E23E0DFE501317BA968A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

072D3D40DFE501317BA668A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

072C9480DFE501317BA468A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

072C4D50DFE501317BA368A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

072C0260DFE501317BA268A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

072BAEF0DFE501317BA168A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

072B57A0DFE501317BA068A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

072AECA0DFE501317B9F68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

072A94C0DFE501317B9E68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

072A0440DFE501317B9C68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

0729B780DFE501317B9B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

072968F0DFE501317B9A68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

0728C760DFE501317B9868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

07287E50DFE501317B9768A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

07283600DFE501317B9668A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

0727ED30DFE501317B9568A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

0727A0B0DFE501317B9468A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

0726F990DFE501317B9268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

07265700DFE501317B9068A86D17958E.description: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.

07260200DFE501317B8F68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

0725AAA0DFE501317B8E68A86D17958E.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.

072502F0DFE501317B8C68A86D17958E.description: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.

0724BAD0DFE501317B8B68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

07241560DFE501317B8968A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

0723B3F0DFE501317B8868A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

07235DF0DFE501317B8768A86D17958E.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

07230230DFE501317B8668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

0722BB10DFE501317B8568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

07222AC0DFE501317B8368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

0721E2E0DFE501317B8268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

0720E2D0DFE501317B7F68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

07208E80DFE501317B7E68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

072047B0DFE501317B7D68A86D17958E.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

071FFF50DFE501317B7C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

071FB050DFE501317B7B68A86D17958E.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

071F1740DFE501317B7968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.

071ECD80DFE501317B7868A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

071E80F0DFE501317B7768A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

071DE4F0DFE501317B7568A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

071D8FE0DFE501317B7468A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

071D4A40DFE501317B7368A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

071C6B50DFE501317B7068A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

071C1C80DFE501317B6F68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

071BBCC0DFE501317B6E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

071B7080DFE501317B6D68A86D17958E.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

071A95B0DFE501317B6A68A86D17958E.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

071A4BC0DFE501317B6968A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

0719F1E0DFE501317B6868A86D17958E.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

07194530DFE501317B6668A86D17958E.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

0718D7E0DFE501317B6568A86D17958E.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

07186640DFE501317B6468A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

07178990DFE501317B6168A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

07174330DFE501317B6068A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

0716F9E0DFE501317B5F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

0716ABC0DFE501317B5E68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

07165440DFE501317B5D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

0715CA10DFE501317B5B68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

071580F0DFE501317B5A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

07153650DFE501317B5968A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

07148E60DFE501317B5768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

07143D10DFE501317B5668A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

0713DB00DFE501317B5568A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

F4521B10DFE401315CFC68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

F451C2F0DFE401315CFB68A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

F4518290DFE401315CFA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

F4513EC0DFE401315CF968A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

F450F8E0DFE401315CF868A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

F450AFB0DFE401315CF768A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

F4506C10DFE401315CF668A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

F4502100DFE401315CF568A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

F44FD5C0DFE401315CF468A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

F44F92C0DFE401315CF368A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

F44F02D0DFE401315CF168A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
comments: For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

F44EBAD0DFE401315CF068A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

F44E6390DFE401315CEF68A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

F44DB450DFE401315CED68A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

F44D6700DFE401315CEC68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

F44D2280DFE401315CEB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

F44CE010DFE401315CEA68A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

F44C9A60DFE401315CE968A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

F44C4CA0DFE401315CE868A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

F44C0CB0DFE401315CE768A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

F44BCAE0DFE401315CE668A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

F44B8510DFE401315CE568A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

F44B3960DFE401315CE468A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

F44AF3E0DFE401315CE368A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

F44AB0A0DFE401315CE268A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

F4498920DFE401315CDE68A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

F4493A30DFE401315CDD68A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.
Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.
F44A5C80DFE401315CE168A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

F44A1610DFE401315CE068A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

F449CEB0DFE401315CDF68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

F44832F0DFE401315CDA68A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

F447F3D0DFE401315CD968A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

F447B4D0DFE401315CD868A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

F4477200DFE401315CD768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
comments: A range of algorithms may be used.

F4472860DFE401315CD668A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.
F446DB60DFE401315CD568A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

F4469740DFE401315CD468A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
comments: This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

F4465460DFE401315CD368A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

F4460F90DFE401315CD268A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

F4456D90DFE401315CD068A86D17958E.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

F44515D0DFE401315CCF68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
Example: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.)

Example: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.)

F444D450DFE401315CCE68A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

F4448E30DFE401315CCD68A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ÷ 3, 6 × 6 = ?.

F4444B40DFE401315CCC68A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

F4440330DFE401315CCB68A86D17958E.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.
comments: For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.

F443BBE0DFE401315CCA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
comments: For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

F4436C10DFE401315CC968A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

F442E0F0DFE401315CC768A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

F4429160DFE401315CC668A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

F44147F0DFE401315CC268A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

F4409F70DFE401315CC068A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

F55318E0DFE401315EB068A86D17958E.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

F552A5C0DFE401315EAF68A86D17958E.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

F5523190DFE401315EAE68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

F551DA60DFE401315EAD68A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

F5517F80DFE401315EAC68A86D17958E.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

F5512480DFE401315EAB68A86D17958E.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

F550BF70DFE401315EAA68A86D17958E.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

F5504D30DFE401315EA968A86D17958E.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

F54FC000DFE401315EA868A86D17958E.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

F54F0B10DFE401315EA668A86D17958E.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

F54EA960DFE401315EA568A86D17958E.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

F54E5590DFE401315EA468A86D17958E.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

F54E0070DFE401315EA368A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

F54DA930DFE401315EA268A86D17958E.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

F54D4F30DFE401315EA168A86D17958E.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

F54CF0E0DFE401315EA068A86D17958E.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

F54C9E40DFE401315E9F68A86D17958E.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.
F54BF4C0DFE401315E9D68A86D17958E.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

comments: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.
F54B99A0DFE401315E9C68A86D17958E.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

F54B3530DFE401315E9B68A86D17958E.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

F54ACD70DFE401315E9A68A86D17958E.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

F54A6230DFE401315E9968A86D17958E.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

F5496630DFE401315E9768A86D17958E.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

F5491540DFE401315E9668A86D17958E.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write <sup>a(x </sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub> in the form q(x) + <sup>r(x)</sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub>, where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

F5487050DFE401315E9468A86D17958E.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.
comments: The Binomial Theorem can be proved by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.

F5481C60DFE401315E9368A86D17958E.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)2 = (x² — y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

F547C510DFE401315E9268A86D17958E.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems

F5476690DFE401315E9168A86D17958E.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

F541DDE0DFE401315E8268A86D17958E.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
4322AB315C124C4F8FC1E1D32E9C46F9.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
BFAE330806214C0FAE9DCBFB40A7E6CF.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

E1D77E31C0134F9B99E653813F7621B5.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
17BDF8D7FB8241D89A1576AFDEEEB5BD.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: District of Columbia Physical Education Standards

130AAC80DFE5013190ED68A86D17958E.description: Discuss factors that influence internal and external motivation and employ motivational techniques to enhance group productivity.

1308A7F0DFE5013190E668A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate and utilize knowledge of psychological and sociological concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activity.

13085D50DFE5013190E568A86D17958E.description: Explain the value of increased flexibility when participating in physical activity and diagram how flexible muscles allow more range of motion in physical activity.

13081E00DFE5013190E468A86D17958E.description: Identify the correct body alignment for performing upper- and lower-body stretches.

1307DEB0DFE5013190E368A86D17958E.description: Determine the intensity of personal physical activity, using the concept of perceived exertion

13079C60DFE5013190E268A86D17958E.description: Describe the short- and long-term benefits of maintaining a healthy body composition.

13071250DFE5013190E068A86D17958E.description: Discuss the need for oxygen and fuel to be available during ongoing muscle contraction so that heat and waste products are removed.

1306BBA0DFE5013190DF68A86D17958E.description: Discuss how body temperature and blood volume are maintained during physical activity, when an adequate amount of water is consumed.

13067140DFE5013190DE68A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply the principles of overload in safe, age-appropriate activities.

13062730DFE5013190DD68A86D17958E.description: Explain the principles of physical fitness: frequency, intensity, time, and type.

13059BF0DFE5013190DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify which muscles are used in performing muscular endurance activities.

130557A0DFE5013190DA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the difference between muscular strength and muscular endurance.

13050650DFE5013190D968A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between the heart and lungs during physical activity.

1304C410DFE5013190D868A86D17958E.description: Identify the heart rate intensity (target heart-rate range) that is necessary to increase aerobic capacity.

13043350DFE5013190D668A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness concepts, principles, and strategies to improve health and performance.

1303F300DFE5013190D568A86D17958E.description: Develop a two-week personal physical fitness plan specifying the proper warm-up and cool-down activities and the principles of exercise for each component of health-related physical fitness.

1303B1F0DFE5013190D468A86D17958E.description: Participate in physical activity a minimum of four days each week and measure and evaluate changes in health-related physical fitness based on physical activity patterns.

130317C0DFE5013190D268A86D17958E.description: Develop individual goals for each of the components of health-related physical fitness; periodically assess the attainment of, or progress toward these goals; and make necessary adjustments to a personal physical fitness program.

13029A30DFE5013190D068A86D17958E.description: Measure and record changes in aerobic capacity and muscular strength, using scientifically based health-related physical fitness assessments.

13021A40DFE5013190CE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the proper form for stretching the back, neck, abducts, hip flexors and adductors, and calves.

130187E0DFE5013190CC68A86D17958E.description: Perform abdominal curl-ups; modified, traditional, and triceps push-ups with hands on a bench; oblique curl-ups on each side, forward lunges, and side lunges to enhance endurance and increase muscle efficiency.

13006370DFE5013190C868A86D17958E.description: Students assess and maintain a level of physical fitness to improve health and performance through a physically active lifestyle.

13001D20DFE5013190C768A86D17958E.description: Explain how height and weight affects performance and influences the selection of developmentally appropriate physical activities.

12FFD0F0DFE5013190C668A86D17958E.description: Explain how movement qualities contribute to the aesthetic dimension of physical activity.

12FF85A0DFE5013190C568A86D17958E.description: Diagram and demonstrate basic offensive and defensive strategies for individual and dual physical activities.

12FF46E0DFE5013190C468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate body management and object-manipulation skills needed for successful participation in introductory adventure/outdoor activities.

12FF0480DFE5013190C368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate body management and locomotor skills needed for successful participation in track and field and competitive activities.

12FEC1E0DFE5013190C268A86D17958E.description: Explain and demonstrate spin and rebound principles for performing manipulative skills.

12FE7C30DFE5013190C168A86D17958E.description: Provide feedback to a partner to assist in developing and improving movement skills.

12FDEB30DFE5013190BF68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of movement concepts, principles, and skills that apply to the learning and performance of a variety of physical activities.
