02AEBC80DFE5013173D268A86D17958E.description: Select a grouping of their own works of art that reflects growth over time and describe the progression based on the same criteria.

02AE5320DFE5013173D168A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply specific criteria alone or in groups to assess and critique works of art.

02ADE0E0DFE5013173D068A86D17958E.description: Develop and discuss possible theories about the artist's intent in a series of works of art, using reasoned statements to support personal opinions (e.g., Jacob Lawrence's Migration Series, Phillips Collection; Claude Monet's Rouen Cathedrals, National Gallery of Art).

02AD76F0DFE5013173CF68A86D17958E.description: Present a reasoned argument about the artistic value of a work of art after viewing a museum reproduction. Respond to the arguments put forward by others within a classroom setting.

02AD0CA0DFE5013173CE68A86D17958E.description:
Verbalize interpretations of aesthetic valuing in writing and speaking about works of art, including judgment (determination of the degree of merit and whether the work is successful):
  • Subject
  • Composition
  • Content
  • Description
  • Analysis
  • Interpretation
  • Judgment

02AC0680DFE5013173CC68A86D17958E.description: Respond to, analyze, and make judgments about works in the visual arts. (Aesthetics, Valuing & Perspectives of Art)

02AB9E80DFE5013173CB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the message of major works of art created by women during identified times. Describe the societal impact of those works. Utilize internet research and site visits (e.g., Primary sources can be viewed at the National Museum of Women in the Arts).

02AB38C0DFE5013173CA68A86D17958E.description: Identify and discuss the classical influences in the monuments and special buildings of the Federal Government in Washington, DC.

02AA5C20DFE5013173C868A86D17958E.description: Investigate the origin and/or preservation history of a historic site, a subway station, or public work of art through a site visit. Recognize how artists/designers can change the public's perception of a space.

02A97DB0DFE5013173C668A86D17958E.description: Explain the function and meaning of works of art from its historical perspective.

02A8F400DFE5013173C568A86D17958E.description: Compare, contrast, and analyze styles of art from a variety of early, colonial and contemporary America, drawing on a museum visit and research.

01E876B0DFE50131720968A86D17958E.description: Create - Understand and create choreographic forms and meaning in dance.

document.title: District of Columbia Science Standards

0B20DCB0DFE5013182FB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that people have a wide but not unlimited range of external features, such as differences in their size, shape, and color of hair, skin, and eyes.

0B2097B0DFE5013182FA68A86D17958E.description: Observe that and describe how offspring are very much, but never exactly, like their parents and like other offspring of the same parents.

0B204CD0DFE5013182F968A86D17958E.description: Explain that humans, like all living things, reproduce offspring of their own kind.

0B200A20DFE5013182F868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and discuss that people are more like one another than they are like other animals. Each type of animal is more like its relatives (family) than it is like the animals of other types (or families).

0B1FCAD0DFE5013182F768A86D17958E.description: Humans have predictable life cycles. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1F88B0DFE5013182F668A86D17958E.description: Describe that plants and animals in our city have habitats that are essential to their survival. For instance, the schoolyard is a habitat that provides the basic needs for a variety of plants and animals.

0B1F41C0DFE5013182F568A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the many kinds of organisms that lived in the past that are now extinct (have died out), and explain how these organisms were similar to, and others very different from, organisms that are alive today.

0B1EEFF0DFE5013182F468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the numbers and types of living things can vary greatly from place to place.

0B1EA6E0DFE5013182F368A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that living things are found almost everywhere in the world in habitats such as the oceans, rivers, rainforests, mountain ranges, arctic tundra, farms, cities, and other environments. Recognize that some habitats are extreme, such as the very deepest parts of the oceans or inside hot springs.

0B1E62D0DFE5013182F268A86D17958E.description: Many different types of plants and animals inhabit the Earth. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1E1E30DFE5013182F168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that most microorganisms do not cause disease and many are beneficial (e.g., yeasts, bacteria of the soil).

0B1DD5D0DFE5013182F068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there is a vast world of living things, called microorganisms, too small to see with the unaided eye.

0B1D7750DFE5013182EF68A86D17958E.description: Cite examples of how animals and plants sometimes cause changes in their surroundings. While some of these changes are easy to see, some are very small and hard to recognize, even though they can be very important.

0B1D2480DFE5013182EE68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe how the local environment (water, dry land) supports a wide variety of plants and animals, some unique to the Chesapeake Bay.

0B1CD750DFE5013182ED68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that materials in nature, such as grass, twigs, sticks, and leaves, can be recycled and used again, sometimes in different forms, as birds do in making their nests.

0B1C9520DFE5013182EC68A86D17958E.description: Observe and explain that plants and animals both need to take in water, animals need to take in food, and green plants need light.

0B1C5330DFE5013182EB68A86D17958E.description: Explain that food for almost all kinds of animals can be traced through a food web back to green plants.

0B1C1030DFE5013182EA68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe how animals may use plants, or even other animals, for shelter and nesting.

0B1BC870DFE5013182E968A86D17958E.description: Living things depend on one another and their environment for survival. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1B7D20DFE5013182E868A86D17958E.description: Observe and cite examples of how some animals and plants change their appearance as the seasons change.

0B1B3900DFE5013182E768A86D17958E.description: Observe and identify the visible, external features of plants and animals and describe how these features help them live in different environments.

0B1AEF50DFE5013182E668A86D17958E.description: Plants and animals have structures that serve different functions in growth, survival, and reproduction. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1A4C80DFE5013182E468A86D17958E.description: Investigate and explain how water left in an open container seems to disappear into the air (evaporation), but water in a small, closed container does not disappear.

0B19F830DFE5013182E368A86D17958E.description: Describe when water is frozen into ice and the ice is allowed to melt, the amount of water is the same as it was at the beginning.

0B19AAA0DFE5013182E268A86D17958E.description: Explain how water can be transformed from one state to another by adding or taking away heat energy.

0B1967D0DFE5013182E168A86D17958E.description: Investigate and explain that water, like many other substances, can be a liquid, a solid, or a gas, and it can transform from one state to another.

0B192340DFE5013182E068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that materials can be manipulated to change some of their properties (e.g., cooling or heating).

0B18D980DFE5013182DF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that solids have a definite shape; liquids and gases take the shape of their containers.

0B189660DFE5013182DE68A86D17958E.description: Materials come in different states, including solids, liquids, and gases. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1802D0DFE5013182DC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how discarded products contribute to the problem of waste disposal and how recycling and reuse can help solve this problem.

0B17C420DFE5013182DB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain how certain materials — such as recycled paper, cans, and certain types of plastic containers — can be used again.

0B178590DFE5013182DA68A86D17958E.description: The Earth's resources can be conserved. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B174720DFE5013182D968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific examples of how human beings protect themselves from adverse weather conditions through different means.

0B170860DFE5013182D868A86D17958E.description: Describe the differences among the various forms of precipitation (rain, snow, sleet, and hail).

0B16C720DFE5013182D768A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between weather and climate.

0B1683F0DFE5013182D668A86D17958E.description: Describe and chart that the temperature and amounts of rain or snow vary in the same months in each place every year.

0B163390DFE5013182D568A86D17958E.description: Investigate and compare weather changes from day to day and place to place.

0B15E7C0DFE5013182D468A86D17958E.description: Explain that air temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, and precipitation make up the weather in a particular place and time.

0B159860DFE5013182D368A86D17958E.description: Explain how weather patterns occur continually on Earth.

0B154580DFE5013182D268A86D17958E.description: Weather can be observed, measured, and described. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B21ACD0DFE5013182FE68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how our lives would be different without such technologies as automobiles, computers, and electric motors.

0B216D30DFE5013182FD68A86D17958E.description: Although each of the human enterprises of science and technology has a character and history of its own, each is dependent on and reinforces the other. As a basis for understanding this concept, students:

0B1211F0DFE5013182C868A86D17958E.description: Make simple line and bar graphs (e.g., track daily changes in outdoor air temperature).

0B149A30DFE5013182D068A86D17958E.description: Explain that sometimes a person can make general discoveries about a group of objects or organisms, such as insects, plants, or rocks, by studying just a few of them, even though the group may vary in details. Understand that this is not inconsistent with the existence of biological variation.

0B144860DFE5013182CF68A86D17958E.description: Explain that some events can be predicted with near certainty, such as a sunrise and sunset, and some cannot, such as storms.

0B140900DFE5013182CE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that people are more likely to believe ideas when they are supported by observations.

0B13C820DFE5013182CD68A86D17958E.description: Draw pictures and write brief, coherent descriptions that correctly portray key features of an object.

0B138340DFE5013182CC68A86D17958E.description: Measure objects in standard units and include units in reports of measurements with simple calculations (e.g., 3 cm + 3 cm = 6 cm).

0B133CD0DFE5013182CB68A86D17958E.description: Use tools, such as thermometers, magnifiers, rulers, or balances, to investigate, observe, measure, design, and build things.

0B12C350DFE5013182CA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to work with a team, but still reach and communicate one's own conclusions about findings.

0B126110DFE5013182C968A86D17958E.description: Make new observations when there is disagreement among observers or among successive observations.

0B11C870DFE5013182C768A86D17958E.description: Describe objects as accurately as possible and compare observations with those made and reported by others.

0B117E80DFE5013182C668A86D17958E.description: Scientific progress is made by asking relevant questions and conducting careful investigations. As a basis for understanding this concept, and to address the content in this grade, students should develop their own questions and perform investigations. Students:

document.title: District of Columbia Health Education Standards

10E10DF0DFE501318D4368A86D17958E.description: Predict how decisions regarding various health behaviors have consequences for oneself.

10E06B50DFE501318D4168A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to implement decision-making and goal-setting skills to enhance health.

10E01530DFE501318D4068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between negative and positive behaviors used in conflict situations (e.g., name calling and hitting vs. trying to see the other person's point of view and compromising).

10DF8A70DFE501318D3E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to show respect for others by the way one behaves, talks, and touches, including how not to interrupt or talk when someone else is talking.

10DF4DE0DFE501318D3D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how friends can feel angry and sometimes hurt one another, yet remain friends.

10DF1000DFE501318D3C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics needed to be a responsible family member and friend, such as being a person who helps, shares, listens, and is kind and polite.

10DED1B0DFE501318D3B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to match nonverbal communication with verbal communication to express feelings.

10DE50B0DFE501318D3968A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to utilize interpersonal communication skills to enhance and protect health.

10DE0430DFE501318D3868A86D17958E.description: Explain how media advertisements encourage children to want certain types of products (e.g., free prizes) by using cartoon characters, catchy phrases, famous people, or other strategies.

10DD7130DFE501318D3668A86D17958E.description: Describe how families show love for each other and how changes in a family (e.g., births, divorce, employment changes, illnesses, deaths) may make its members feel happy or sad.

10DCDDD0DFE501318D3468A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to analyze the influence of family, culture, media, and technology on health and health behaviors.

10DC9730DFE501318D3368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between a good/safe touch, a bad/unsafe touch and a confusing touch; and explain what to do if touching causes uncomfortable feelings.

10DC4810DFE501318D3268A86D17958E.description: Understand that one's body is one's own and that no one has the right to touch another in a way that makes the other feel uncomfortable.

10DC0B10DFE501318D3168A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate basic traffic and pedestrian safety skills needed to avoid injury (e.g., crossing streets, bicycle safety).

10DB8E30DFE501318D2F68A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate self-care practices that promote cleanliness and hygiene, such as correct handwashing, regular bathing, and washing clothes.

10DB0B20DFE501318D2D68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to apply self-management skills to enhance personal health and safety.

10DAB900DFE501318D2C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of common signs, symbols, and warning labels.

10DA5A30DFE501318D2B68A86D17958E.description: Identify parents, teachers, and doctors as people who provide valid health information.

10D9DF30DFE501318D2968A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the ability to access and evaluate health information, products, and services.

10D9A140DFE501318D2868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the differences between helpful medicines and harmful drugs.

10D95F10DFE501318D2768A86D17958E.description: Discuss how first- and second-hand cigarette smoke impact the environment and the health of oneself and others.

10D770F0DFE501318D2068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between healthy and unhealthy food choices and how they might lead to becoming overweight or obese.

10D8D4A0DFE501318D2568A86D17958E.description: Summarize how many childhood illnesses can be prevented or treated (e.g., by hand washing, immunizations, not sharing cups or combs, covering coughs and sneezes).

10D84A60DFE501318D2368A86D17958E.description: Describe the benefits of getting adequate sleep (e.g., to aid in the growth and repair of the body).

10D809F0DFE501318D2268A86D17958E.description: Name and locate the basic body organs, including the heart, brain, lungs, skin, and stomach, and describe their functions.

10D6D8D0DFE501318D1E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how a clean school, home, and community environments prevent the spread of germs.

10D691B0DFE501318D1D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the need for rules to promote safety, and explain how decisions to follow or disregard safety guidelines have consequences for self and others.

10D60F00DFE501318D1B68A86D17958E.description: Explain differences between various emotions; and describe constructive methods to accommodate a variety of feelings, including the feelings of others.

10D57E90DFE501318D1968A86D17958E.description: Students comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention.

document.title: District of Columbia Physical Education Standards

12A260E0DFE50131903668A86D17958E.description: Contribute ideas and listen to the ideas of others in cooperative problem-solving activities.

12A1E050DFE50131903468A86D17958E.description: Include others in physical activities and respect individual differences in skill and motivation.

12A15750DFE50131903268A86D17958E.description: Accept responsibility for one's own performance without blaming others.

12A0CC70DFE50131903068A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate and utilize knowledge of psychological and sociological concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activity.

12A06920DFE50131902F68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between effective and ineffective warm-up and cool-down techniques.

12A02700DFE50131902E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the elements and purpose of warm-up and cool-down activities.

129FE9B0DFE50131902D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how strengthening major muscles can improve performance at work and play.

129F6DE0DFE50131902B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effect of regular, sustained physical activity on the body's ability to consume calories and burn fat for energy.

129EE150DFE50131902968A86D17958E.description: Explain how technology can assist in obtaining physical fitness.

129E9CF0DFE50131902868A86D17958E.description: Explain why the body needs water before, during, and after physical activity.

129E1A70DFE50131902668A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness concepts, principles, and strategies to improve health and performance.

129DD910DFE50131902568A86D17958E.description: Meet age- and gender-specific fitness standards for aerobic capacity, muscular strength, flexibility, and body composition, using a scientifically based health-related fitness assessment.

129D95D0DFE50131902468A86D17958E.description: Measure and record changes in aerobic capacity and muscular strength, using scientifically based health-related physical fitness assessments.

129D0020DFE50131902268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to warm-up and cool-down muscles and joints before aerobic activities such as running, jumping, kicking, throwing, and striking.

129C7890DFE50131902068A86D17958E.description: Hang by the hands from an overhead bar with the hips and knees each at a 90-degree angle.

129BF460DFE50131901E68A86D17958E.description: Calculate personal heart rate per minute by recording heartbeats for ten-second intervals and fifteen-second intervals.

129BA010DFE50131901D68A86D17958E.description: Participate in continuous moderate to vigorous physical activities a minimum of three to four days each week that require sustained movement of the large muscle groups to increase breathing and heart rate.

129AF680DFE50131901B68A86D17958E.description: Identify healthful choices for meals and snacks that help improve physical performance.

129A99D0DFE50131901A68A86D17958E.description: Set personal short-term goals for aerobic endurance, muscular strength and endurance, and flexibility, and monitor progress by measuring and recording personal fitness scores.

129A2F30DFE50131901968A86D17958E.description: Participate in physical activity a minimum of four days each week and measure and evaluate changes in health-related physical fitness based on physical activity patterns.

12999580DFE50131901768A86D17958E.description: Students assess and maintain a level of physical fitness to improve health and performance through a physically active lifestyle.

129953C0DFE50131901668A86D17958E.description: Explain the similar movement elements of the underhand throw and the underhand volleyball serve.

129911B0DFE50131901568A86D17958E.description: Manipulate an object by using a long-handled implement and contrast that with using a short-handled implement.

1298D130DFE50131901468A86D17958E.description: Describe the appropriate body orientation to strike a ball, using the forehand movement pattern.

12989020DFE50131901368A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between offense and defense and determine the spacing between offensive and defensive players based on the speed of the players.

12984E70DFE50131901268A86D17958E.description: Describe and create ways to maintain or increase the spacing between two players quickly.

12980840DFE50131901168A86D17958E.description: Perform simple partner balance stunts while sharing a common base of support.

12977810DFE50131900F68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of movement concepts, principles, and skills that apply to the learning and performance of a variety of physical activities.

129738A0DFE50131900E68A86D17958E.description: Volley a tossed lightweight ball, using the forearm pass and identify key body positions used for volleying a ball.

1296B140DFE50131900C68A86D17958E.description: Keep a foot- or hand-dribbled ball away from a defensive partner and contrast that with dribbling a ball without a defender.

12961A80DFE50131900A68A86D17958E.description:
Kick:
  • a ball to a moving partner, using the inside of the foot
  • a stationary ball from the ground into the air.

12957A70DFE50131900868A86D17958E.description: Throw and catch an object with a partner while both partners are moving.

12953160DFE50131900768A86D17958E.description: Catch a fly ball above the head, below the waist, and away from the body and explain and demonstrate the correct hand position.

1294DCE0DFE50131900668A86D17958E.description:
Throw:
  • overhand at increasingly smaller targets, using proper follow-through
  • a flying disc for distance, using the backhand movement pattern
  • (serve) a lightweight ball to a partner, using the underhand movement pattern.

12943970DFE50131900468A86D17958E.description:
Strike a gently tossed object or ball with:
  • a paddle or racket
  • a bat, using a side orientation.

129398D0DFE50131900268A86D17958E.description: Perform a routine to music that includes complex locomotor patterns.

12930C10DFE50131900068A86D17958E.description: Jump a single rope for a specified amount of time for purposes of endurance.

1292C900DFE501318FFF68A86D17958E.description: Turn and jump two ropes simultaneously (i.e., Double Dutch).

12923840DFE501318FFD68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

06F9DD40DFE501317B5168A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

06F98FC0DFE501317B5068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

06F948F0DFE501317B4F68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).

06F90160DFE501317B4E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

06F8B7F0DFE501317B4D68A86D17958E.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

06F86DB0DFE501317B4C68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

06F814D0DFE501317B4B68A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

06F7CC20DFE501317B4A68A86D17958E.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

06F78160DFE501317B4968A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.

06F64200DFE501317B4568A86D17958E.description: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

06F5F010DFE501317B4468A86D17958E.description: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).

06F543B0DFE501317B4268A86D17958E.description: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.

06F4EEF0DFE501317B4168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

06F49160DFE501317B4068A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.

06F43C80DFE501317B3F68A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

06F3F180DFE501317B3E68A86D17958E.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

06F3A9F0DFE501317B3D68A86D17958E.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).

06F35F70DFE501317B3C68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.

06F30CB0DFE501317B3B68A86D17958E.description: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.

06F2B8E0DFE501317B3A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

06F1DD40DFE501317B3768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

06F193D0DFE501317B3668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

06F14600DFE501317B3568A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

06F0AB10DFE501317B3368A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

06F00420DFE501317B3168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

06EFA700DFE501317B3068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

06EF0380DFE501317B2E68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

06EE9EA0DFE501317B2D68A86D17958E.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

06EE2AF0DFE501317B2C68A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.

06EDDC60DFE501317B2B68A86D17958E.description: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.

06ED3C60DFE501317B2968A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

06ECF140DFE501317B2868A86D17958E.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

06ECA7E0DFE501317B2768A86D17958E.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

06EC5F00DFE501317B2668A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

06EC1070DFE501317B2568A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

06EB0C50DFE501317B2268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

06EAB650DFE501317B2168A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

06EA68E0DFE501317B2068A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

06E9C7B0DFE501317B1E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

06E97D80DFE501317B1D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

06E92B70DFE501317B1C68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

06E889C0DFE501317B1A68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

06E744D0DFE501317B1668A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

06E6F210DFE501317B1568A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).

06E68530DFE501317B1468A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

06E618F0DFE501317B1368A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

06E5C330DFE501317B1268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

06E4D800DFE501317B0F68A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

06E48050DFE501317B0E68A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

06E43730DFE501317B0D68A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is…).

06E33F20DFE501317B0A68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

06E29A10DFE501317B0868A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

06E250A0DFE501317B0768A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

06E208A0DFE501317B0668A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

06E1BDA0DFE501317B0568A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

06E17340DFE501317B0468A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

06E11870DFE501317B0368A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

06E0A070DFE501317B0268A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

06DFFA90DFE501317B0068A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

06DFB2C0DFE501317AFF68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

06DF67A0DFE501317AFE68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

06DEBE60DFE501317AFC68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

06DE7790DFE501317AFB68A86D17958E.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

06DDDD60DFE501317AF968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

06DD7FC0DFE501317AF868A86D17958E.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

06DD2DE0DFE501317AF768A86D17958E.description: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

06DCE640DFE501317AF668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sound for each consonant.

06DC9F00DFE501317AF568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

06DC0F00DFE501317AF368A86D17958E.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

06DBC000DFE501317AF268A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonent-vowel-consonent, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.)

06DB6710DFE501317AF168A86D17958E.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

06DB2000DFE501317AF068A86D17958E.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

06DA8D00DFE501317AEE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

06D9F2B0DFE501317AEC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

06D98D40DFE501317AEB68A86D17958E.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

06D918D0DFE501317AEA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

06D8ABD0DFE501317AE968A86D17958E.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

06D85D70DFE501317AE868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

06D73B00DFE501317AE568A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

06D6F400DFE501317AE468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

06D6A930DFE501317AE368A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

06D65C30DFE501317AE268A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

06D604D0DFE501317AE168A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

06D56A20DFE501317ADF68A86D17958E.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

06D51BE0DFE501317ADE68A86D17958E.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

06D4CDC0DFE501317ADD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

06D42FE0DFE501317ADB68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

06D3E490DFE501317ADA68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

06D399F0DFE501317AD968A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

06D29A40DFE501317AD668A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

06CC5C60DFE501317AD568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

06CC1490DFE501317AD468A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

06CB8580DFE501317AD268A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

06CAF040DFE501317AD068A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

06CA9870DFE501317ACF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

06CA4500DFE501317ACE68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

06C99560DFE501317ACC68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

06C94320DFE501317ACB68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

06C8F110DFE501317ACA68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

06C7F5A0DFE501317AC768A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

06C7A910DFE501317AC668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

06C76080DFE501317AC568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

06C713B0DFE501317AC468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

06C6B420DFE501317AC368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

06C61C20DFE501317AC168A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

06C5CC10DFE501317AC068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

06C572A0DFE501317ABF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

06C4C350DFE501317ABD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

06C47370DFE501317ABC68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

06C422C0DFE501317ABB68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

06C36A20DFE501317AB968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: District of Columbia Arts Education Learning Standards

01A356A0DFE50131720668A86D17958E.description: Invite a local artist to work on a project in the school. Recognize how an artist plans a project, prepares materials, executes the project, involves the school community, extends learning and makes a positive impact on the learning environment.

01A2F1C0DFE50131720568A86D17958E.description: Identify professions in or related to the visual arts and some of the specific skills needed for those professions e.g. studio artist, art educator, web designer, stone mason, architect, curator, museum educator.

01A222E0DFE50131720368A86D17958E.description: Examine art, photography, and other two- and three-dimensional images in order to compare how different visual representations of the same object lead to different interpretations of its meaning, and describe or illustrate the results.

01A15200DFE50131720168A86D17958E.description: Research and present the ways art illustrates and/or commemorates historical people and events through sculpture, paintings, photographs, and maps.

01A0DEB0DFE50131720068A86D17958E.description: Use various drawing skills and techniques to depict lifestyles and scenes from selected civilizations.

01A061C0DFE5013171FF68A86D17958E.description: Use mathematical ratios and proportions to represent the human figure.

019FEB40DFE5013171FE68A86D17958E.description: Study the music and art of a selected historical era and create a multimedia presentation that reflects that time and culture.

019F7D20DFE5013171FD68A86D17958E.description: Construct a book (using book arts) combining text and illustration using the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, editing/proofreading, publishing/presenting), that summarizes information.

019E8840DFE5013171FB68A86D17958E.description: Connect and apply what is learned in the visual arts to other art forms, subject areas, visual culture and communications and to careers. (Connections, Relationships, Applications)

019E21C0DFE5013171FA68A86D17958E.description: Identify changes in a personal work of art and explain how those changes improved the work.

019DBFB0DFE5013171F968A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply specific criteria individually or in groups to assess and critique works of art in writing.

019D5980DFE5013171F868A86D17958E.description: Explain the intent of a personal work of art and draw possible parallels between it and the work of a recognized artist.

019CECE0DFE5013171F768A86D17958E.description:
Construct an interpretation of a work of art based on aesthetic valuing vocabulary-description (size, medium, process, subject, elements), analysis (how the work is organized, facts about the elements and principles), interpretation (the meaning, mood, message or idea the viewer feels the artist is trying to communicate):
  • Subject
  • Composition
  • Content
  • Description
  • Analysis
  • Interpretation

019C0E40DFE5013171F568A86D17958E.description: Respond to, analyze, and make judgments about works in the visual arts. (Aesthetics, Valuing & Perspectives of Art)

019B98F0DFE5013171F468A86D17958E.description: Explain how objects made for functional, ritual, and other purposes are considered art in different contexts.

019B21B0DFE5013171F368A86D17958E.description: Relate works of art to varying styles and genres to the periods in which they were created (e.g., Bronze Age, Ming Dynasty, Renaissance, Classical, Modern, Post-Modern, Contemporary, Futuristic, others). Use museum internet research and museum observation for research.

019AB280DFE5013171F268A86D17958E.description: Research and describe how art and architecture can reflect cultural values in traditions throughout the world.

019A4B50DFE5013171F168A86D17958E.description: Participate in a DC sponsored art event; recognize how painting a mural or reclaiming a public space helps to transform a neighborhood and improves the quality of life.

0199E240DFE5013171F068A86D17958E.description: Relate works in the arts chronologically to historical events (e.g., 10,000 B.C to present), including a graphic benchmark timeline.

01996AE0DFE5013171EF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the main function and meaning of works of art from Ancient Civilizations and the Middle East (e.g., ancient Greece, the Persian Empire, Egypt, Rome, India, China, and the Silk Road).

01990530DFE5013171EE68A86D17958E.description: Historical Development, Role and Cultural Diversity of the Visual Arts

01989F90DFE5013171ED68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and understand historical and cultural dimensions of the visual arts and to construct meaning in the diverse ways in which human experience is expressed across time and place. (Historical and Cultural Context)

01983910DFE5013171EC68A86D17958E.description: Use contemporary technologies to create original works (e.g., film, photography, computer graphics, or video).

0197D220DFE5013171EB68A86D17958E.description: Create symmetrical designs using rotation, reflection and/or translation shapes on a measured grid.

01976380DFE5013171EA68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate reality and fantasy in a work of art.

01967F40DFE5013171E868A86D17958E.description: Select a medium to use to communicate a theme in a series of works of art.

01960CF0DFE5013171E768A86D17958E.description: Expression Through Original Works of Art

01959A70DFE5013171E668A86D17958E.description: Maintain the workspace, materials, and tools responsibly and safely.

01953570DFE5013171E568A86D17958E.description: Using congruent triangles and area measurement create a patterned design (e.g. quilt)

0194CDD0DFE5013171E468A86D17958E.description: Mix paints and show color relationships.

01945D70DFE5013171E368A86D17958E.description: Use various shading methods in a drawing to show light and shadow (e.g. hatching, crosshatching, stippling, and blending).

0193BF60DFE5013171E268A86D17958E.description: Use scaled proportion in a drawing of forms (e.g., cube, cylinder, cone, and pyramid).

01934E80DFE5013171E168A86D17958E.description: Apply the rules of 2-point perspective to show the illusion of depth on a two-dimensional surface, using overlapping shapes, relative size, and placement within the picture (e.g. landscape, cityscape).

019276E0DFE5013171DF68A86D17958E.description: Apply artistic processes and skills in a variety of media to communicate meaning and intent in original works of art. (Production and Creative Expression)

01920730DFE5013171DE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret reality and fantasy in original two-dimensional and three-dimensional works of art. Visit the National Gallery of Art and discuss Renee Magritte and a Salvador Dali style at the National Museum of African Art.

019195C0DFE5013171DD68A86D17958E.description: Visit a museum/gallery to view work of the Washington Color School. (e.g. Corcoran Gallery, National Gallery)

01911620DFE5013171DC68A86D17958E.description: Search the internet to identify and compare how artists create the illusion of space in a variety of art works.

0190A930DFE5013171DB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the ways in which artists convey the illusion of space (e.g., placement, overlapping, relative size, atmospheric, and linear perspective). View the art of Jacob Lawrence, Maurice Prendergast, and Honoré Daumier at The Phillips Collection.

019038A0DFE5013171DA68A86D17958E.description: Develop a working understanding of line drawing techniques. Interpret the technical characteristics of a drawing, such as proportion and internal ratios.

018FD7F0DFE5013171D968A86D17958E.description: Introduce the rules of 2 point perspective in comparison to 1 point perspective in drawings.

018F71F0DFE5013171D868A86D17958E.description: View and describe ways subject matter is depicted.

018F0820DFE5013171D768A86D17958E.description: Identify, name, and describe scale and proportion as applied to two-dimensional and three-dimensional works of art.

018E9AF0DFE5013171D668A86D17958E.description: Analyze various shading techniques used by artist (e.g. hatching, crosshatching, blending, and stippling) in drawings.

018E0B20DFE5013171D568A86D17958E.description: Identify drawing media (e.g. charcoal, conte' crayon, pen and ink) and discuss how different media are used to achieve different effects.

018DA480DFE5013171D468A86D17958E.description: Develop perceptual skills, analyze elements of art and the principles of design

018D42D0DFE5013171D368A86D17958E.description: Perceive and understand the components of visual language: the elements of art and the principles of design. (Artistic Perception)

018C7260DFE5013171D168A86D17958E.description: Research and report on the theatrical traditions of different cultures over time, such as those in Egypt, Ancient Greece, Medieval Japan, China, and West Africa.

018C0C60DFE5013171D068A86D17958E.description: Use theatrical skills to present concepts or ideas from other curriculum areas (e.g., creating a musical based on a piece of literature) and explain how theatre enhances an understanding of that subject area.

018BA940DFE5013171CF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how cultural influences affect the content or meaning of works of theatre.

018B47B0DFE5013171CE68A86D17958E.description: View different productions of the same scene and compare and contrast its portrayal through various mediums (e.g., video, film, and live performances).

018AE490DFE5013171CD68A86D17958E.description: Apply theatrical concepts to construct meaning and understanding in other subject areas.

018A7520DFE5013171CC68A86D17958E.description: Develop criteria and write a formal review of a theatrical production incorporating elements such as script, actors, design, and direction.

0189FC60DFE5013171CB68A86D17958E.description: Explore the theatrical elements of a ritual within a culture that marks a "rite of passage".

01897140DFE5013171CA68A86D17958E.description: Critique design elements of theatre productions as they relate to tone, mood, time, and place.

0188F3E0DFE5013171C968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate variation in pitch, stress, and tempo to convey mood and characterization in theatre productions.

01888390DFE5013171C868A86D17958E.description: Use the vocabulary of theatre, such as playwright, rehearsal, dress rehearsal, run-through, and cold-reading to describe theatrical experiences.

018818F0DFE5013171C768A86D17958E.description: Analyze, critique, and respond to theatre and dramatic media.

0187B010DFE5013171C668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to participate cooperatively in the different tasks required to create a theatrical production, including assisting with some of the technical equipment of theatre.

01874A00DFE5013171C568A86D17958E.description: Explain how scenery, lighting, sound, costumes and makeup work together to create a theatrical environment.

0186DE50DFE5013171C468A86D17958E.description: Design and create masks, puppets, props, costumes, or sets in a selected theatrical style drawn from world cultures.

01867840DFE5013171C368A86D17958E.description: Analyze and research a play to make design choices about theatrical environments and articulate the rationale for all artistic choices.

018613F0DFE5013171C268A86D17958E.description: Design and manage theatrical environments for formal and informal dramatizations.

0185A500DFE5013171C168A86D17958E.description: Create scripts that include characters, actions, and scenes that exhibit tension and suspense.

01852700DFE5013171C068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate projection, vocal variety, diction, gesture, and confidence in an oral presentation.

0184B2C0DFE5013171BF68A86D17958E.description: Make acting choices when developing scenes that employ cause and effect, problem-solving, and alternative resolutions to dramatic conflict through the element of plot.

018443C0DFE5013171BE68A86D17958E.description: Write, direct, and perform scenes or short plays that include monologue, dialogue, action, and environment together with a range of character types.

0183D520DFE5013171BD68A86D17958E.description: Perform and participate in theatre improvisations and dramatizations to learn acting and scriptwriting fundamentals.

0182E9D0DFE5013171BB68A86D17958E.description: Associate aural examples of music to a variety of cultures, styles, and historical periods.

018215A0DFE5013171B968A86D17958E.description: Research career and vocational options in music using available technology.

0181A760DFE5013171B868A86D17958E.description: Analyze concepts common to music and other disciplines.

01807610DFE5013171B568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast materials being studied in its historical and cultural context, including music from the 20th and/or 21st century.

017F7110DFE5013171B368A86D17958E.description: Research career and vocational options in music using available technology.

017F0610DFE5013171B268A86D17958E.description: Discuss relationships between music concepts and other disciplines.

017DBEF0DFE5013171AF68A86D17958E.description: Describe distinguishing characteristics of representative choral music from a variety of cultures.

017D26B0DFE5013171AE68A86D17958E.description: Classify an exemplary vocal/choral work by music style.

017C4230DFE5013171AC68A86D17958E.description: Explore careers in music and relate them to careers in the other fine and performing arts.

017BDC80DFE5013171AB68A86D17958E.description: Examine and evaluate characteristics of various arts from a particular historic period and various cultures, using appropriate terms.

017A8900DFE5013171A868A86D17958E.description: Associate distinguishing characteristics of representative choral music from a variety of cultures.

017A1270DFE5013171A768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the functions of vocal/choral music in various cultures.

01794290DFE5013171A568A86D17958E.description: Explore careers in music and relate them to careers in the other fine and performing arts.

0178D750DFE5013171A468A86D17958E.description: Associate common music elements and descriptive terms with those used in art, dance, and drama.

01778120DFE5013171A168A86D17958E.description: Connect music to other art forms and subject areas through understanding the historical and cultural context of music.

01770710DFE5013171A068A86D17958E.description: Read and notate rhythmic and melodic notation.

0176A4E0DFE50131719F68A86D17958E.description: Use a symbol system to sight-read melodies in major and minor keys.

01763F30DFE50131719E68A86D17958E.description: Sight-read individual voice parts in a vocal score.

01756E90DFE50131719C68A86D17958E.description: Read and notate rhythmic and melodic notation.

01750380DFE50131719B68A86D17958E.description: Use a symbol system to sight-read melodies in major keys.

01749E00DFE50131719A68A86D17958E.description: Sight-read individual voice parts in a vocal score.

0173CD70DFE50131719868A86D17958E.description: Read and notate rhythmic patterns in various meters at various tempi.

017356C0DFE50131719768A86D17958E.description: Sight-read, analyze and practice simple phrases of up to eight measures using music notation.

01726F00DFE50131719568A86D17958E.description: Sight-read, analyze and practice simple phrases of up to four measures using music notation.

01712B60DFE50131719268A86D17958E.description: Compose a selection for two or more voices making use of available technology.

0170C440DFE50131719168A86D17958E.description: Improvise a melody to a 12 bar blues, iii-VI-ii-V, and ii- V7-I chord progression in various key centers.

016FE660DFE50131718F68A86D17958E.description: Create harmonies for a given melody.

016F8190DFE50131718E68A86D17958E.description: Compose rhythmically interesting melodies within specified guidelines.

016F1D40DFE50131718D68A86D17958E.description: Improvise a melody to a 12 bar blues and ii-V7-I chord progression.

016E4B60DFE50131718B68A86D17958E.description: Create harmony for a given melody.

016DD6A0DFE50131718A68A86D17958E.description: Compose rhythmically interesting melodies within specified guidelines.

016D6740DFE50131718968A86D17958E.description: Embellish a folk song by creating rhythmic and melodic variations based on I, IV, and V (V7) chords.

016C84E0DFE50131718768A86D17958E.description: Compose rhythmic patterns and simple melodies within specified guidelines.

016C1AB0DFE50131718668A86D17958E.description: Improvise "responses" in a similar style to given rhythmic and melodic phrases.

016BB530DFE50131718568A86D17958E.description: Create variations of familiar melodic phrases on a neutral syllable.

016A74F0DFE50131718268A86D17958E.description: Play an accompaniment to a voice part on a melodic instrument.

document.title: Next Generation Science Standards

6032D6F445374B0CA32F2DA5E3CE4F08.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

1E95D64661AD4A4FA76DC8BF11E1EBF5.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

E6C43EFA22324C19B3335D89117027F0.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

BA047CD300F44D498CC8568F70D9EB7C.description: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of design solutions to weather-related hazards could include barriers to prevent flooding, wind resistant roofs, and lighting rods.

5BE10D7502BC44C68D9FADD5EEF2F150.description: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data could include average temperature, precipitation, and wind direction.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of graphical displays is limited to pictographs and bar graphs. Assessment does not include climate change.
7B80534E127A44988535FA7144B84225.description: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.

55CD433F446A4AB09D6BFB562806F5F8.description: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of environmental changes could include changes in land characteristics, water distribution, temperature, food, and other organisms.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to a single environmental change. Assessment does not include the greenhouse effect or climate change.

69A3219E6A0C46F1B159FB06C2ABB520.description: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence could include needs and characteristics of the organisms and habitats involved. The organisms and their habitat make up a system in which the parts depend on each other.

62E8BF97C23046FFA04D9FB126711EFC.description: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of cause and effect relationships could be plants that have larger thorns than other plants may be less likely to be eaten by predators; and, animals that have better camouflage coloration than other animals may be more likely to survive and therefore more likely to leave offspring.

E2E4AEA206414DEC933BF4C1FB407D22.description: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data could include type, size, and distributions of fossil organisms. Examples of fossils and environments could include marine fossils found on dry land, tropical plant fossils found in Arctic areas, and fossils of extinct organisms.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include identification of specific fossils or present plants and animals. Assessment is limited to major fossil types and relative ages.

Clarification Statement: Examples of the environment affecting a trait could include normally tall plants grown with insufficient water are stunted; and, a pet dog that is given too much food and little exercise may become overweight.
45BF599BB8B84618965E0A044A637A86.description: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.

54F70691465F4207A87763478CF99F10.description: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Patterns are the similarities and differences in traits shared between offspring and their parents, or among siblings. Emphasis is on organisms other than humans.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include genetic mechanisms of inheritance and prediction of traits. Assessment is limited to non-human examples.

1AA59465372D45ACB264A471BF201D76.description: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

013B060813E742A7AB0F1FC0BB06405A.description: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.

comments: Clarification Statement: Changes organisms go through during their life form a pattern.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of plant life cycles is limited to those of flowering plants. Assessment does not include details of human reproduction.
2D3C5E594A0241309DF7C2587BB95CB8.description: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction, and death.

2F5D69D85F464015BEC1FD44684E2C72.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

D8234F380D50444D8D209FD9E561863D.description: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of problems could include constructing a latch to keep a door shut and creating a device to keep two moving objects from touching each other.

Clarification Statement: Examples of an electric force could include the force on hair from an electrically charged balloon and the electrical forces between a charged rod and pieces of paper; examples of a magnetic force could include the force between two permanent magnets, the force between an electromagnet and steel paperclips, and the force exerted by one magnet versus the force exerted by two magnets. Examples of cause and effect relationships could include how the distance between objects affects strength of the force and how the orientation of magnets affects the direction of the magnetic force.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to forces produced by objects that can be manipulated by students, and electrical interactions are limited to static electricity.
C17AFFB918F34B0B911BEF2610965322.description: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.

EBDDB42C53924E60A69E1A895E13787F.description: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of motion with a predictable pattern could include a child swinging in a swing, a ball rolling back and forth in a bowl, and two children on a see-saw.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include technical terms such as period and frequency.

0F65E14FC2054ED3B35EE19FE2986B3F.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples could include an unbalanced force on one side of a ball can make it start moving; and, balanced forces pushing on a box from both sides will not produce any motion at all.

Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to one variable at a time: number, size, or direction of forces. Assessment does not include quantitative force size, only qualitative and relative. Assessment is limited to gravity being addressed as a force that pulls objects down.

110D3D0A1E094BCB9A91CC70580F68F8.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
